My Virginia Tech vs. SMU prediction backs Mustangs quarterback Kevin Jennings to extend drives when the Hokies' pass rush brings heat, making SMU laying the points my top pick tonight. At the same time, Ethan Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech's aerial attack provide a viable path to the full-game Over, regardless of whether SMU secures the victory. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p. m. ET tonight, Friday, Nov. 6, on ESPN, with Kalshi showing a 66% win probability for the Mustangs. Read on for my free college football picks for tonight's Week 10 slate. TOP PICK Who will win Virginia Tech vs SMU: SMU -5.5 Play the SMU Mustangs to cover -5.5 at 54% or less. SMU has a more reliable path to multiple touchdown drives than the Virginia Tech Hokies . The Mustangs succeed on 50.4% of offensive snaps, ninth nationally , and QB Kevin Jennings generates 0.31 EPA per dropback. Virginia Tech's fifth-ranked havoc rate can wreck a possession, but it still allows successful plays on 43.4% of snaps . The Hokies can't count on a sack or takeaway to end every drive, and with Jennings' ability to avoid sacks, the task for a havoc-reliant team becomes much more difficult. At the other end, Virginia Tech's ground game produces a near-negative EPA per rush, inviting SMU to put Ethan Grunkemeyer in obvious passing situations. The bye helps the Hokies' preparation, but keeping this within five requires them to disrupt Jennings repeatedly while sustaining enough drives of their own. I expect SMU's offensive edge to produce a full-touchdown margin. Virginia Tech vs SMU Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 Play the Over 55.5 at 53% or less. SMU's defense allows 4.58 points per opponent scoring opportunity, 112th nationally . That gives Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech a route to points even if they can't control the game. The Hokies have thrown effectively enough to threaten downfield, while SMU's defense has been better at preventing long drives than finishing stops once opponents cross the 40. On the other side, the Mustangs produce explosive plays on 9.9% of snaps, eighth nationally . Their scoring doesn't have to consume much clock. I expect SMU to set the pace and Virginia Tech to contribute enough through the air to clear this full-game number. Virginia Tech vs SMU prop: SMU Team Total over 30.5 I like the Mustangs to score here and I'd play this to 60% Virginia Tech's havoc is a legitimate obstacle, but SMU has been unusually good at rescuing drives: it ranks second nationally with 0.57 EPA per play on third and fourth down . Jennings can punish a defense that gets aggressive without ending the possession and he's hard to do that against. Tech also allows a successful play on 44.6% of opposing dropbacks, giving the Mustangs chances to throw through pressure rather than repeatedly challenge its front. Kendrick Raphael's eight rushing touchdowns give SMU a dependable option near the goal line. Virginia Tech vs SMU combo I like this combo because Virginia Tech should be healthier up front. James Franklin said the bye should bring offensive linemen Montavious Cunningham and Brody Meadows back. Better protection gives Grunkemeyer more time to find Que'Sean Brown and makes 24 Virginia Tech points plausible without requiring a road win. SMU can answer quickly enough for a productive first half, while the moneyline leaves room for the Hokies to keep it close. (Photo by Matthew Visinsky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Steve Helwick · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Time and date: Friday, November 6 at 7:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-6) Over/under: 56.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 2-1 Last meeting: SMU 28, Virginia Tech 25 — September 21, 1974 Current streak: SMU, 2 (1973-74) Setting the scene While No. 1 Miami (FL) and No. 14 Wake Forest are the only ACC teams that reside in the AP Top 25, the conference title race is far from finished. There are five two-loss teams lurking right behind, and two of them clash Friday night in Dallas. It's the first meeting between SMU and Virginia Tech as ACC opponents, however, it's a familiar head coaching matchup: Rhett Lashlee and James Franklin stood on opposite sidelines as recently as 2024 in the College Football Playoff. There's plenty on the line for the bowl eligible opponents. A win would do wonders for remaining in the ACC race, especially for SMU, which can still capture a tiebreaker against Wake Forest. But a third conference loss is essentially an elimination in a 17-team league. Virginia Tech Hokies outlook BLACKSBURG, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 17: Head coach James Franklin of the Virginia Tech Hokies greets Kaleb Spencer #3 before the game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets at Lane Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Blacksburg, Virginia. (Photo by Michael Shroyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) can make another statement on the road after its bye week. The Hokies haven't rattled off seven wins in a regular season since 2019, but that streak could end Friday in year one of the James Franklin era. Virginia Tech is fresh off its biggest win under Franklin, taking down Clemson 20-16 in Death Valley on Oct. 24. Close games have been commonplace for the Hokies this season. Each of their last six contests were decided by 10 points or fewer. Three featured lead changes in the final five minutes, while another ended on a missed field goal attempt that would have resulted in a lead change. The restoration of Virginia Tech football can be attributed to the passing game. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer followed Franklin from Penn State and has drastically improved in his junior campaign. Grunkemeyer has connected on an efficient 71.4 percent of attempts — seventh nationally among quarterbacks with 100 attempts — and has delivered 17 touchdowns against two interceptions. Grunkemeyer has eclipsed 300 yards three times and finished seven of his eight starts without throwing a pick. Two receivers have carried a bulk of the load. Wide receiver Que'Sean Brown ranks atop the team with 51 receptions and 685 receiving yards, and he's secured at least five receptions in all eight games. Tight end Luke Reynolds has also been a matchup nightmare for defenses. Reynolds' 50 receptions rank first and his 491 receiving yards ranks third among all FBS tight ends. While a bulk of his production occurred in September, his outing against Clemson was a productive one, snagging two touchdowns on seven receptions. The Hokies aren't as adept in the run game, where they check in at 111th in the FBS with 3.7 yards per carry. They don't incorporate much quarterbaack mobility and primarily rely on the duo of Jeffrey Overton Jr. and Marcellous Hawkins Jr. Overton, a common weapon in the receiving game, showed the extent of his powers in a 209-yard rushing explosion against Boston College. Hawkins has been a steady secondary back, and he's tied for the team lead with five rushing touchdowns. Virginia Tech only surrendered more than 26 points once this season, and that was a Friday night matchup against Pittsburgh. The Hokies' defense has been a positive for the team, tied for 35th in points allowed and ranked 27th in yards allowed per game. Their strength involves limiting the run, where they give up just 93.4 yards per game on a 3.0 average. Sacks heavily factor into that total, and Virginia Tech is the best in the ACC and the sixth-best in the nation at getting to the quarterback, producing 3.4 sacks per game. It's a defensive end led effort. Aycen Stevens ranks first in the conference with 8.0 sacks, while his fellow defensive ends Cortez Harris and Mylachi Williams have 5.0 and 4.5, respectively. The Hokies haven't been as strong on the back end, but they prevent explosive plays well. No team has recorded a 50-yard completion on this defense all season. But what Virginia Tech needs to improve upon is its turnover output. The Hokies forced just five takeaways through eight games, causing the team to enter Friday with a minus-4 in the turnover battle this season. SMU Mustangs outlook DALLAS, TX - OCTOBER 17: Southern Methodist University Mustangs defensive end Marques White (16) rushes the passer during the game between SMU and Virginia on October 17, 2026 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by George Walker/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images SMU (6-2, 4-2 ACC) dropped from the rankings after a heartbreaking 30-27 loss at Syracuse last weekend. It was only the Mustangs' fourth conference defeat since joining the ACC, and the third in which they held a lead in the final minute. However, SMU has never lost back-to-back ACC games and owns an 11-0 record in ACC play at home, giving Rhett Lashlee's team the perfect opportunity to bounce back and remain in the conference title race. Slow starts have been the Mustangs' kryptonite. In their last five ACC games, they haven't scored more than 13 points in a half or entered the break with a lead larger than three. However, they've won each of their last five second halves, finishing a plus-68 over that span. SMU's offense is led by Kevin Jennings, who is one of seven passers averaging over 300 yards per game. This season has been a masterclass in efficiency for the senior, who is completing passes at a 73.7 percent clip — the third-highest rate in the country among quarterbacks with 100 attempts. Jennings has also thrown 152 consecutive passes without an interception, with his last misfire coming in the first quarter of a Sept. 26 matchup against Missouri State. The Mustangs' receiver room is as deep as they come, with five different players over the 200-yard threshold. Yamir Knight is the leader with 44 receptions for 523 yards, while Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale can also pose as explosive threats for an offense that ranks fifth nationally in 50+ yard receptions. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrstrom are also incorporated into the passing game, and they tie for the team lead with four receptions apiece. Unlike SMU's first ACC defeat at Louisville, last Saturday's loss to Syracuse was largely determined in the trenches. The Mustangs uncharacteristically allowed six sacks, accounting for 43 percent of their season total. Additionally, they struggled to create space for the running backs, which never broke off an explosive gain. Kendrick Raphael has posted three 100-yard games already in ACC play, and he can also do damage out of the backfield as a receiving option. SMU's defense didn't necessarily have a bad outing at Syracuse, limiting the Orange to 5.9 yards per passing attempt and 3.7 yards per rush. But the Mustangs surrendered conversions on all four of Syracuse's fourth down attempts, allowing the Orange to sustain otherwise lost drives. A veteran defensive line full of super seniors is the strength of the unit. SMU ranks 15th nationally with 2.9 sacks per game, and eighth-year senior Marques White leads the way with 5.5 sacks, while the rest of the sacks are quite evenly distributed. The pressure goes hand-in-hand with a strong passing defense, and SMU ranks 28th nationally in fewest passing yards allowed at 182 per game. That is the most improved element of the Mustangs from last year, but losing starting strong safety Tyren Polley for the year could make things difficult down the road. Sael Reyes stepped up last game with 10 tackles in his second start of the season, while Jimmy Wyrick recorded eight from the other safety spot. Lastly, turnovers have been a significant determinant in SMU results this season. The Mustangs lost the turnover battle 5-0 in their two losses, and they're the only bowl eligible team at a minus-5 or worse this season. These 6-2 teams are structured somewhat similarly: strong passing attacks with tight end utilization, dominant defensive fronts that repeatedly get to the quarterback, and solid defenses hampered by poor turnover margins. Short weeks oftentimes favor the home team, and SMU remains perfect against ACC opponents at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Given SMU's discrepancy between first and second half performance, Virginia Tech may enter halftime with the lead, but the Mustangs ultimately rally behind Kevin Jennings in the fourth quarter to secure a one-score win on The Hilltop. Prediction: SMU 30, Virginia Tech 24

picks.blurb: Virginia Tech Hokies vs. SMU Mustangs: News, Information, and Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL trade deadline grades Latest CFP rankings Tatum, Celtics rout Brown, Sixers NFL trade deadline tracker Vikings trade for Cousins Virginia Tech Hokies vs. SMU Mustangs: News, Information, and Predictions Stike up the Hokie Pokey, Tech Triumph, and the Victory Tag. | John Schneider - SB Nation John Schneider · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:59 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's a short week after a week break. The Hokies are heading to Dallas to face off against the Southern Methodist University Mustangs. The Hokies are up against another major ACC opponent, and winning the game means advancing in the ACC and potentially seeing a ranking. Crossover Week Mayhem Just a note from us: Well, the first week in November through the first week of December is always a challenge for coverage. The soccer teams are wrapping up with decent enough records, but their seasons aren't quite over. The Women's Basketball Team has opened their home record at 2-0, and the Men's team also graced Cassell with a W. All of that puts a real strain on coverage so bear with us as we sort out schedules, and fight fall health issues and work vs. Hokie sports balance. The football team isn't finished, though. There are still four games left on the schedule, and then we get to plan on bowl coverage this season. Isn't that a happy event? The Hokies are bowl eligible just a couple of games after the halfway point, and that's a very pleasant occurrence. To think that we are actually paying attention to the bowl invitation list, instead of worrying on Thanksgiving weekend whether or not a win will net an invitation somewhere. The first thing to cover is a bit of fun. The ACC Network desk hosts Eric McClain and Eddie Royal had a bet going. Remember, McClain is a former Clemson player, and we all know and love Eddie Royal. So, the bet was that the loser had to wear the winner's mascot costume. Eddie was not dressed as a Tiger with the googly eyes for the TV segment. ( Congratulations to the Virginia Tech Cheer Squad equipment folks and Travis Wells for getting most of an actual Hokie Bird big enough for Eric. ) The Virginia Tech Wrestling Team received a massive boost from a wrestler who hasn't even wrestled his first match as a Hokie, yet, but who is already a world champion. Freshman Bo Bassett traveled to Kazakhstan and netted the program its first world championship and was the first American in 20 years to win in his weight class (65KG – for those lacking metric conversion skills that's 143 pounds ). The Coach Robie is going to have an absolutely dominant wrestling team this season. Back to Football Stuff It looks like the team is going to be wearing head to toe all-whites for this one. Go get your coffee, or a quick snack and listen in on Coach Franklin's weekly presser. As Bryan posted up earlier, this time the Hokies have some really good news coming out of the locker room as it pertains to the Offensive Line. Montavious Cunningham and Brody Meadows are back up to speed and are expected to play on Friday night. The O-Line has been dipping into the #3s on the depth chart for the past few games, and getting them back is a serious update to the struggling run game. That All Leads to This… Predictions The SMU Mustangs are largely a Big XII import with a near automatic bubble to the top of the ACC football pile. It's Dallas, TX, and football is a near religion for Texas. That means the program is well funded, with premium coaching, and players doused liberally with NIL funding. Up until last weekend, the Mustangs were sporting a very respectable one loss record. Until they showed up in the Syracuse (whatever they call the Carrier Dome, now), as expected in the beginning of the season SMU was challenging hard for the #2 bid in the ACC fake Championship game ( until the conference goes back to divisions and division champs who play everyone else in the division the game in Charlotte will remain fake to me ). Then the Mustangs got treated to the old Big East upset win by the Orange. That knocked them down a peg but also put the Hokies in the position of earning the #3 spot on the ACC leader board. That all means that this game might not mean an ACC bid, but it will mean a much better bowl game situation over the holidays. Bowls mean big broadcast money, and the program needs the cash to make up for a restricted gate at Lane. The Mustangs are favored by slightly less than a touchdown for this one, in their house no less. We'll see how we feel about that. This is a big test for the Hokies. Virginia Tech had a huge win at Clemson two weeks ago. No, this isn't the same Clemson team as only a few years ago, but it means something for other ACC teams to walk into Death Valley and win. SMU is better than the Tigers, but they aren't unbeatable. The clear difference here is the quarterback position. SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings is a stud. He also has one of the ACC's best running backs and one of the top receiving units in the league. This is a huge challenge for VT defensive coordinator Brent Pry. Offensively, I think the Hokies have success moving the ball. SMU's size on the defensive interior concerns me, especially with Tech's OL struggles. There is hope that with Cunningham and Meadows back, the offensive line is better, but we'll see. I expect a close game. My heart says the Hokies, my head says SMU in a close one. SMU 34, Hokies 31 This game all depends on how the Mustangs adjusted to their Syracuse loss, and if the Hokies on both sides of the ball can adjust to how the Orange controlled the SMU offense, and how they managed to get by their defense. SMU, interestingly enough, has a similar offensive/defensive balance to Tech's than we have seen this season. There are lots of "IFs" in this game, and the biggest one is "IF" the Tech defense can limit the SMU offense to what it's been scoring over the season against peer teams, the Hokies have a much better chance to win than the listed 6-point betting gimme to SMU. The latest projected O/U is 56.5, which tells me volumes of information. The analysts see this as a very close game, and the end result being less than a full score between the two teams. If the Hokies stay away from getting enamored of the run game and go downfield fast and consistently in the air on quick developing intermediate routes to their best receivers, there will be run opportunities. If Tech decides to try to "establish the run" the offense could bog down into chronic 3-and-outs. The return of two key #1/#2 depth chart players is not an excuse to try to revert to 1960's caveman Johnny Unitas two runs and a pass offense. If the Hokies move the ball and do it fast, they have enough defense ( which needs to put serious pressure on the quarterback on every play ) to hold the Mustangs to a 3.5 score effort. The Hokies are capable of 4 or more. That's a whole lot of "Ifs" though. Here's the skinny… the first team to score over 30 points wins. That puts my prediction hat on, and I think the Hokies might just be good for it, regardless of the conditions. Just a quick reminder of the times and broadcast information. It's an ESPN deal.

Ahead of the clash, here's our staff's predictions as to what will unfold tonight in the Lone Star State. JACKSON CAUDELL: While it will still be a long shot even if they find a way to win, the Hokies' ACC hopes are on the line tomorrow night at SMU. The Mustangs are also battling for their ACC title hopes, and that makes this a fascinating matchup. This is a chance for James Franklin to land another win against one of the better programs in the conference, and I think they have the offense to take advantage of a suspect SMU defense. If the Hokies can get after Kevin Jennings and force a few turnovers, I think they are able to do that and score a big win. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 31, SMU 27 JAMES DUNCAN: Syracuse left a blueprint last Saturday, beating SMU 30-27 on a touchdown with 17 seconds left. Virginia Tech is built to follow it. Nobody has beaten the Hokies by more than five points this season, and they come in with 13 days of rest to SMU's six. Ethan Grunkemeyer has thrown 17 touchdowns and two interceptions, and both picks came in one night against Pitt. He won't hand Kevin Jennings free possessions, which puts the game on Brent Pry's defense. That group made 13 tackles for loss at Clemson, and it won't need half that many Friday if it gets off the field on third down. Friday won't be a rout, but I think the Hokies give the Mustangs their first home loss in the ACC. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 30, SMU 28 THOMAS HUGHES: Let's get this out of the way: SMU has never lost an ACC game at home. Its strongest wins at Gerald J. Ford Stadium this season, however, came against Virginia and California - two squads with a combined 7-11 (4-8 ACC) record. The Hokies should be well-equipped to contend with the Mustangs, though SMU signal-caller Kevin Jennings may present Tech with its toughest test of the season yet. Virginia Tech quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer has been stellar this campaign, throwing 17 touchdowns to just two interceptions, and while I expect another strong performance from him, I think SMU narrowly edges Virginia Tech in Dallas tonight. Final score prediction: SMU 31, Virginia Tech 28 KADEN REINHARD: I think this game will be defined by one word over the 60 minutes of action: Intensity. Several factors will fuel that fire: Friday night lights, the Mustangs coming off the Syracuse loss and Tech finding itself back in the receiving-votes category of the AP Top 25. But most importantly, I see both offenses locking into a close-knit battle, as both sides can mend their attacks with a healthy mix of the ground and air attack. Ultimately, I think the Hokies' defense can handle the contest by not allowing SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings to extend many plays outside the pocket, which has been a struggle for the Hokies in recent years. Meyers had never scored for the Orange before that catch. The touchdown beat SMU 30-27 and knocked the Mustangs out of the AP Top 25. Virginia Tech should have that clip on a loop. The Hokies (6-2, 3-2 ACC) visit SMU (6-2, 4-2) at 7 p.m. ET Friday on ESPN. The Mustangs are 5-0 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium this season and 6.5-point favorites. Their defense holds up better against the pass than the run, and its injuries are stacked in the middle of the field. Two of my predictions start there. The third starts with what Syracuse did to Kevin Jennings. 1. Luke Reynolds has his best game since September SMU doesn't give much away through the air. Opponents complete 62.6% of their passes and average 6.0 yards per attempt. The one real hole is at safety. Sophomore Tyren Polley Jr., third on the team with 34 tackles, tore a pectoral muscle in October and is out for the season. SMU has played two games without him: a 59-20 win over Cal and the loss at Syracuse. Help could be coming. Ahmaad Moses, a first-team All-ACC safety in 2025, is questionable after missing the whole season while SMU works on his eligibility. The junior tight end has 50 catches for 493 yards and six touchdowns, and his 50 catches lead all FBS tight ends. The last three games have been quieter: 13 catches for 120 yards since Pitt. Two of those 13 went for touchdowns at Clemson, including the go-ahead score in the fourth quarter. Friday, he clears 100 receiving yards for the third time this season and finds the end zone again. 2. Jeffrey Overton Jr. snaps his 100-yard drought Overton last reached 100 yards on Sept. 26, when he ran for 209 at Boston College, the sixth-highest single-game total in Virginia Tech history. He has 230 yards in four games since and averaged 2.6 yards per carry at Clemson. The sophomore still leads the Hokies with 639 yards on 113 carries. Two things change Friday. The first is the offensive line. "We're going to get some guys back, which is helpful, especially on the offensive line," coach James Franklin said Monday. Guard/tackle Montavious Cunningham and guard Brody Meadows are expected to play. Left tackle Justin Terry is still out. The second is the defense across from him. SMU allows 125.9 rushing yards per game and 3.8 yards per carry. Those numbers flatter the Mustangs. College football counts sacks as rushing plays, and SMU has 23 sacks for 148 yards. Pull them out, and opponents are averaging 4.8 yards per designed run. Those 23 sacks matter for Virginia Tech in another way. Ethan Grunkemeyer has been sacked 23 times himself. A run game that works keeps the Hokies on schedule and gives SMU's rushers something else to think about. Overton gets his third 100-yard game of the season. 3. Virginia Tech sacks Kevin Jennings at least four times Before Halloween, SMU hadn't allowed more than two sacks in a game this season. Syracuse got six. Look at who was playing on the left side. True freshman Drew Evers moved over from right tackle to start at left tackle, and fellow true freshman Sam Utu made his first career start beside him at left guard. It was only the second college game of his career. SMU could get some help back. Guard Alex Woods, a starter, missed Syracuse, and tackle Andrew Chamblee, who has started at both tackle spots, hasn't played since Oct. 17. Neither is on Thursday's availability report. Watch the first series to see who lines up on the left. Either way, Virginia Tech has the rushers to test it. The Hokies average 3.4 sacks per game, sixth in FBS, and three players have more than four: Aycen Stevens with eight, Cortez Harris with five and Mylachi Williams with 4.5. Defensive tackle Kemari Copeland said this week the plan is to "cage" Jennings and take away his scrambles to the right. Friday, the Hokies get to Jennings at least four times. Here are five matchups in the game we're keeping a close eye on. 1. BYU's Biggest Danger BYU's biggest vulnerability remains its struggling rushing attack. Injuries along the offensive line and uncertainty surrounding running back LJ Martin's availability only add to the concern. Utah ranks 22nd nationally in rushing defense, allowing just 101.4 yards per game. If the Utes shut down BYU's ground game, quarterback Bear Bachmeier could face constant pressure in obvious passing situations. But both earned their stripes this time around. Last year, the complaint was a relatively light BYU non-conference schedule. This year, is handing Notre Dame its only loss so far good enough for everyone? Last year, Utah destroyed a bad UCLA team 43-10, but it lost to both BYU and Texas Tech. This year, does giving Arkansas – you know, from the beloved SEC – its worst loss of the season so far (43-10, crazily enough) do it for you? Utah got the respect in the first round of the College Football Playoff rankings with a No. 3 spot. Now the program has to show it can have nice things. There will still be work to do, but win this, and then look out. BYU vs Utah: Quick Hits BYU is No. 9 in the first College Football Playoff rankings. Two of the last three games are at home, starting with Baylor next week. Utah goes on the road to Arizona and TCU after this, and closes with West Virginia. BYU won the last three meetings, including 24-21 last year. Utah won nine in a row before that, going back to 2009. It's No. 4 in the nation in fewest sacks allowed, giving up just five this year, and it leads all of college football in fewest tackles for loss given up, getting hit for just 17. For all of the fantastic things Utah does, it doesn't get into opposing backfields. This is where the Cougars have to be patient. Utah loves to control games with long drives, lots of third down conversions, and winning the time of possession battle. Who was the one team that did a decent job on the ground against the Cougar defense? BYU gave up a season-high 170 rushing yards in the loss to UCF. They would lose control of their own destiny if they don't beat Utah. On the other hand, a win over Utah could propel BYU into the top five and in the drivers seat for a spot in the CFP. To win this game, BYU needs to keep the game close in the first quarter. The Utes have outscored their opponents by more than 70 points and have not allowed a touchdown in the first quarter. Utah has scored touchdowns on its opening drive in seven out of eight games. Utah offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven has been brilliant with his opening scripted drives. If BYU can settle in and adjust to Utah's unique offense, the Cougars will have a great chance to pull off the upset. BYU is expected to get LJ Martin back in the lineup for the first time since early October against TCU. How effective and how healthy Martin will be remains to be seen. On offense, Bear Bachmeier will have to carry another heavy load. Bachmeier will have chances to throw from clean pockets against a Utah defense that will give up explosive plays through the air. Bachmeier and his wide receivers, particularly deep threat Legend Glasker, need to have a big game. BYU is the best defense Utah will have faced by a wide margin. Even though the BYU defense has struggled to bring ball-carriers to the ground, we like their chances to keep the Utah offense somewhat in check. Here is how I'm wagering college football Week 10. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . No. 9 BYU @ No. 3 Utah This Holy War might be the holiest of them all: Utah hosting bitter rival BYU, with the winner in the driver's seat for a Playoff spot. It’s the first time both teams have been ranked in the top 10 for this matchup, and I can’t wait to start the day with this one. I think BYU might win outright. It has been tested with its win over Notre Dame just a few weeks ago. Yes, it lost to UCF the following week in a typical trap game — big home win followed by a road conference game. Otherwise, the Cougars have handled business, even though the scores don’t seem that impressive. BYU is built on defense. It is 13th in yards per play and it limits explosives. It does not rush the passer all that well, but against Utah’s rushing attack, that might not be needed. BYU’s defense already faced a high-powered offense in the Irish and limited it to a negative EPA rushing day. Utah’s offensive production slowly ticked down when conference play started, but it did bounce back last week against a poor Cincinnati defense. Utah has played one defense in the same realm as BYU and that was Houston. Utah struggled to score, only putting up 21 points with seven of those happening super late after forcing a Houston turnover. Will the BYU offense find a groove against Utah? (Getty Images) It’s fair to also believe BYU’s offense might struggle in this game. However, it appears the Cougars are getting stud running back LJ Martin back, and they are much better when Martin is on the field. He’s averaging almost eight yards a carry with 20% of his rushes going for 10+ yards. Utah’s defense is the typical physical front against the run, but BYU is the best offense the Utes have faced all season. Utah’s pass rush concerns me. It is 80th in pressure rate and unless it blitzes, it isn't able to get to the quarterback. Seems less than ideal against BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier. I see these teams as even. They are both defensively based with an offense that wants to run the ball. That’s too many points in a game like this. I’ll take BYU to cover. Schwartz's Pick: BYU -4.5 No. 5 Alabama @ No. 14 LSU In the newly-released CFP rankings, Alabama is fifth and is an underdog at LSU by almost a touchdown. I do lean towards LSU at -6, but that number feels big. Instead, I’m going to fade Alabama’s offense in this game. Alabama is facing its fourth straight difficult defense, and in the first three games, we’ve seen the offensive efficiency drop. Quarterback Keelon Russell is nearing the end of his first season as a starting quarterback, and he’s been mostly excellent for his age. However, he has struggled the last three weeks outside the end of the Texas A&M game. Against Georgia, Tennessee and A&M, he completed only 60% of passes with just four passing touchdowns and three interceptions. Alabama’s beat-up offensive line has allowed 11 sacks in the three previous games. Now, the Tide play an LSU defense that’s first in sacks per pressure and 11th in pressure rate. The Bama offensive line and Russell were noticeably affected by the environment in Tennessee, and now they are at LSU. I feel most comfortable with Alabama not scoring much in this game. Rotoworld Player News NFL Player News Fantasy Sports Rotoworld Home Betting Betting Home Profile Login Vaughn Dalzell , Vaughn Dalzell The Big 12 is heating up, and the conference’s biggest game of the year takes place this Saturday at Rice-Eccles Stadium between #9 BYU (7-1) and #3 Utah (8-0). It’s the Holy War! Both teams sit atop the Big 12, and the winner of this game is likely in the Big 12 Championship, whereas the loser can’t afford another loss to make the conference title game. Utah is enjoying its highest ranking in program history, and depending on what happens this weekend, the Utes could end up No. 1. Devon Dampier has led an electric offense averaging 38.9 points per game (11th) in their first year without Kyle Whittingham and with Morgan Scalley at the helm; but the defense has been incredible! The Utes have been a tank from the start. Utah averages 10.3 first-quarter points per game (T-4th) and allows 0.9 (1st) defensively. Utah has gassed up opponents early and carried a lead late; that’s been their M.O. Utah is on the nation’s longest winning streak, 14 games, after thrashing Cincinnati 49-25. The last loss came against BYU 24-21 last season. Utah can get revenge and, in the same breath, claim control of their destiny and the Big 12. If BYU loses to Utah, the Cougars’ college football hopes will rely on winning the Big 12 Championship. With a loss to UCF, BYU put their season on thin ice as Utah, BYU, and Texas Tech battle for the top two spots. BYU had a strong first half against Arizona State last week, leading 17-3 at the break, but was outscored 17-10 in the second half. BYU could get a boost this week with star running back and 2025 Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year LJ Martin returning. Martin has missed the last four games and put a lot of the offensive pressure on Bear Bachmeier . While reports say Martin won’t be 100 percent if he plays, at least he could be a decoy that sets up Bachmeier in RPO or the downfield pass game. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch BYU vs Utah Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Time: 12:00 PM Eastern Site: Rice-Eccles Stadium City: Salt Lake City, UT TV/Streaming: ESPN | ABC Game Odds for Utah vs BYU The latest odds as of Thursday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Utah Utes (-198), BYU Cougars (+164) Spread: Utah -5.5 (-105) Total: 48.5 points Head Coach: Morgan Scalley 2026 Record: 8-0 (5-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 38.9 (11th) Defensive Points Per Game: 15.8 (15th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 83rd 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 34th The Utah Utes Offense: After scoring a season-low 21 points in the win over Houston, Utah scored a season-best against P4 programs, putting up 49 points against Cincinnati. The Utes had 27 first downs, converted 7-of-11 third downs, posted 534 yards of offense, and averaged 6.4 yards per carry. Utah scored a ridiculous 42 points in the first half and led 42-6 at the half. The Utes scored on all four of their offensive drives in the first half, and the defense recorded a pick-six and fumble return for a touchdown. The Utes didn’t score on the first four drives of the second half, but it didn’t make much of a difference; the damage was already done to the Bearcats. Utah enters hot and ready for a shootout at 10 AM their time! Utah Player to Watch on Offense: QB Devon Dampier For the third time in the last four games, Devon Dampier threw three touchdown passes and 200-plus yards in seven straight. Dampier’s been on fire, and even when he’s not slinging touchdowns, he’s running for them. Dampier had 150 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Houston, then turned around and threw for three scores on Cincinnati. In the last four games, Dampier has 12 total touchdowns to one interception and averaged 309.5 total yards in that span, with Utah scoring 34.5 points per game. The Utes have been a tank, and if they win this game, Dampier can jump into the top five odds for the Heisman. The Utah Utes Defense: Utah’s defense has been one of my favorite units to watch this season. They fly around and lay the boom on opponents from the opening drive. Utah allowed over 200 yards in the first half, but Cincinnati couldn’t convert in the red zone, nor on the money downs. Cincinnati went 3-of-13 on third and fourth downs and only managed a 24:30 time of possession. It was a dominant performance from Utah, and in the first quarter, they’ve been the best team all season. Utah’s defense has allowed six total first-quarter points all season and a 0.9 first-quarter points-per-game average, which leads the country. Getting off to a quick start seems impossible for opponents this season; let’s see what BYU can do. Utah Player to Watch on Defense: DB Jackson Bennee In Utah’s biggest game of the season, Jackson Bennee posted a season-high eight tackles, had a sack, forced and recovered a fumble against Houston, then recorded four tackles against Cincinnati the following week. Bennee ranks third on the Utes with 36 tackles, third in pass deflections (4), and tied for the team lead in interceptions (2). Bennee led the team in picks last year (4) and was second in tackles (63), so he’s off to another strong season. BYU has at least stayed consistent with scoring: 24, 28, 31, and 27 points during that span. However, the rushing yardage has decreased each game and has lost the turnover battle 6-2 in that span, with at least one turnover in every game. Bear Bachmeier rose to Heisman candidacy after beating Notre Dame with four touchdowns, but after the loss to UCF and a seven-point win over Arizona State, he’s on the outside looking in. A win at Utah would help his case in a weekend where the Heisman Trophy race will have major chaos. BYU ranks 42th in passing grades per PFF and Utah is 47th in coverage grades, so that will be the biggest battle, outside of these massive offensive lines clashing in the trenches. BYU Player to Watch on Offense: RB LJ Martin LJ Martin has missed the last four games, and in that span, BYU has run for 177, 121, 116, and 47 rushing yards without Martin. Last season, Martin ran for 1,305 yards and 12 touchdowns, plus added 255 receiving yards on 35 catches. Martin was hurt against TCU, and the game prior, he posted a season-high 176 rushing yards and three touchdowns against Colorado State. Whether he is or is not 100 percent, Martin can be utilized in the red zone and short-yardage situations, plus the senior would be a great decoy for play-action early. The BYU Cougars Defense: BYU’s defense had one of its best first-half showings of the season against Arizona State. The Cougars held the Sun Devils to 107 yards and three points in the first half, but the second half was a different story. BYU gave up two straight touchdown drives of 12 and 13 plays for 81 and 39 yards. After that, a punt and field goal pulled the game within seven. BYU played the second half very conservatively in order to hold onto the win and come out healthy. BYU had six sacks, 8 TFL, and forced two fumbles. It was a bounce-back performance, to say the least, after allowing 463 yards to UCF and a season-high 39. BYU Player to Watch on Defense: LB Cade Uluave After 26 tackles over the last three games, Cade Uluave is the team’s leading tackler with 52. Uluave had seven tackles and a sack against Arizona State last week after 10 tackles in the loss to UCF. Uluave led Cal last year with 97 tackles, was second in sacks (3.5), and fourth in pass deflections (4). Uluave has been a four-year starter in college and is an Utah native (South Jordan, UT). This will be a memorable game for Uluave; playing in his first and only Holy War. away.blurb: News Sports Autos Entertainment Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Big 12 availability report lists BYU RB LJ Martin as 'doubtful' Jeremy Mauss BYU Cougars Wire Nov. 5, 2026, 12:33 p.m. ET Hear this story The first availability report is out for the anticipated BYU vs. Utah game. All eyes on the injury report are on Cougars running back LJ Martin. He has slowly making his way back to play , including even being back on the field . Then there are reports from ESPN's Pete Thamel who is not all that confident Martin will play . Now, with the official report out, Martin is officially listed as doubtful. Honestly, that makes sense. Just two weeks ago, Martin was seen wearing a large walking boot when BYU was on the road facing UCF. More availability reports will come out before game day, so this is something to watch. The Tigers (6-2, 3-2 SEC) have already blown out league foes Florida and Texas A&M at home this season and are 13-3 at Faurot Field against league opposition since 2023. Taking on Texas (6-2, 3-2) represents an uptick in competition, but the Tigers shouldn't be lacking confidence. Florida was No. 8 in the AP poll when it arrived at Mizzou on Oct. 3. It left with a 45-17 loss that legitimized Missouri and showed its full potential. Since then, we've also seen Missouri's floor, which was found in a 31-3 loss at Ole Miss on Oct. 17. But after a bye week and a 34-10 "get right" win over Arkansas in Week 9, the Tigers appear to be back on track. The Longhorns are entering off wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State , but their vaunted offense is still falling short of expectations. Is this the point when everything will start to click for quarterback Arch Manning ? If a Texas team that spent four weeks at No. 1 earlier this season is going to meet expectations, a breakthrough needs to come soon. Where to watch Texas vs. Missouri live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Faurot Field -- Columbia, Missouri TV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Texas vs. Missouri: Need to know Injuries mount for Texas: Injuries are adding up for the Longhorns, who enter this matchup with star receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman listed as questionable. Wingo is dealing with a quad injury while Coleman is working through a shoulder issue. Both have appeared in all eight games for Texas up to this point while combining to catch 11 of Arch Manning's 15 touchdown passes. Star edge rusher Collin Simmons is also questionable after missing Texas' past two games because of an ankle injury. That's a lot of star power in the "questionable" category for Texas. By contrast, Missouri's injury report is nearly clean. Welcome back, Ahmad: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy made his 2026 debut last week, carrying the football twice in the Tigers' win over Arkansas. The 2025 All-American has been on the mend from a gunshot wound, and his return adds to a running back room that already features the SEC's leading rusher. Jamal Roberts became the conference's first back to surpass 1,000 yards for the season while rushing for 138 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in a win over Arkansas. Roberts surpassed 200 yards in wins over Florida and Texas A&M last month. Gaining traction against Texas will be tough. No team has averaged more than four yards per rush attempt against Texas. College Football playoff implications: Texas' chance to reach the College Football Playoff will improve to 67.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFB Forecaster. They will drop to 22.8% with a loss. If the Longhorns lose, they would need to win out against LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M in order to potentially reach the 12-team field as a three-loss team. Missouri's chances to make the CFP will improve to 16.1% with a win. Those hopes would crater to 1.6% with a loss. The Tigers close with Georgia , Kentucky and Oklahoma . Texas vs. Missouri prediction, picks The best unit on this field is the Texas defense. Regardless of the health status of star edge rusher Collin Simmons, the Longhorns should be able to slow down a Missouri offense that hasn't faced a swarming unit of this caliber. If Arch Manning can just take care of the football like he did last week, Texas can lean on its defense, win the field position battle and put stress on a Missouri defense that showed real vulnerability in losses to Mississippi State and Ole Miss. The Tigers have been great at home the last few years, but they are a rung below Texas in overall talent level. Staff Picks and Scores Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB After getting to play their entire October slate in the Lone Star State, the Longhorns are once again leaving town for Columbia, Missouri, to take on the No. 18 Missouri Tigers. While fans may already be looking ahead to next week's highly anticipated Death Valley matchup, the Tigers are certainly not a team to overlook . They're coming off a 34-10 blowout win over Arkansas — albeit, it was against the Razorbacks — and steamrolled the same Florida team that stunned Texas with a second-half comeback just a few weeks ago. Saturday's matchup carries significant postseason implications , both for the College Football Playoff and the SEC championship race, as both teams enter with identical 3-2 conference records. Here’s how the Texas Longhorns On SI Staff sees this one playing out. Matt Galatzan Texas has gotten back on track over the last two weeks, but various shortcoming are still very prevelent. Texas has struggled along offensive line, and as a result, the running game has suffered. Those issues have also caused a cascading effect on the passing game, making for an inconsistent product. To make things worse, things on the injury front don't look good for the Horns. Kade Phillips, Ryan Wingo and Graceson Littleton are all banged up but should play, while Colin Simmons and Cam Coleman are less likely to play, and Hollywood Smothers and Nick Townsend were both lost for the year. Texas can overcome these issues if the defense continues to perform at a high level. Ole Miss showed the blueprint to shut down the Tigers ' offense. If Texas can stay on schedule on offense and avoid a third-quarter collapse, I think they can get it done. Texas 27, Missouri 20 Phoenix Haigis Texas has started to find their groove again with two major wins at home against Ole Miss and Mississippi State. The Longhorns now go back on the road against another ranked opponent in Missouri. As much momentum as Texas has going into this game, all the advantages matchup-wise go in favor of the Tigers. Texas is dealing with a significant amount of major injuries with the addition of running back Hollywood Smothers being out for the season while Missouri will see their running back Ahmad Hardy return for the first time this season. The Tigers are one of the best teams at home this year and have the best turnover margin in the SEC against a Lorghorns team that has had turnover issues this season. Although Texas is favored, the math tells a different story and could eliminate the Longhorns’ playoff chances. Zion Trammell Texas and Missouri have the makings of a defensive slugfest. It’ll be a cold morning in Columbia, Missouri, which could challenge the offenses. Both the Longhorns and Tigers rank in the top four in the SEC in average rushing yards allowed per game. Texas may need a big defensive play to win. I think Will Muschamp’s defense will deliver, and the Longhorns will win a close game on Saturday. However, this feels like the Arch legacy game that many have been begging to see. Perhaps it's also because that might be what HAS to happen, but I'm riding with believing in Manning in this one. Oct 31, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns linebacker Rasheem Biles reacts after making a defensive stop during the second half against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Leo Barnes All things considered, I still like this Texas team. This will be a defensive dogfight. It won't be pretty, and it might even be a little boring at times — that is, if all you care about is high-flying action. And while the injury report isn't promising one bit, I still believe this Texas defense can be every bit as legitimate as it's proven itself to be. Stopping Missouri starts with shutting down the run game, and I fully expect Justin Cryer and Rasheem Biles to help answer the call. I could easily see either one leading the team in tackles by the time it's all said and done. Ultimately, Texas' ability to stonewall opposing offenses should be enough to keep the Tigers in check, giving its sometimes-average offense just enough breathing room to squeak out another win. He is also a senior sports reporter for The Daily Texan, where he currently covers the men’s basketball beat. Arch Manning, Austin Simmons NCAAF Texas heads to Columbia with its top two receivers questionable, adding another concern for an offense that's struggled to find its rhythm. My Texas vs. Missouri prediction examines whether the Longhorns can overcome those issues against a dangerous Tigers defense. Missouri is a perfect 4-0 at home and fresh off a convincing 34-10 win at Arkansas. The Tigers know how to get after the quarterback, which could spell trouble for Arch Manning behind a shaky Texas offensive line. I'm taking the points with Missouri and expecting a low-scoring battle in Saturday's SEC showdown. Find out why in my latest college football picks for Week 10. TOP PICK Who will win Texas vs. Missouri: Missouri +2.5 I would play the Missouri Tigers to cover this number down to 52%. The Texas Longhorns ' passing game runs through Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo, and both are questionable after leaving the win over Mississippi State hurt. Coleman hasn't practiced this week. To make matters worse, left tackle Trevor Goosby is out. Arch Manning was already producing -0.04 EPA per dropback with all three of them in the lineup. Missouri's Austin Simmons sits at 0.20 EPA per dropback , and he gets a Texas secondary with two starting corners listed as questionable. Mizzou is 4-0 at home this season, winning those games by an average of 24.8 points. I'll gladly take the team in better form with the better offense. Texas vs. Missouri Over/Under pick: Under 43.5 I'd play the Under to 42.5. Missouri will want to lean on Jamal Roberts, but they own a 37.8% rushing success rate, 128th nationally . That's a rough matchup against a Texas defense allowing a 35.8% rushing success rate, seventh in the country. Missouri also stalls near the goal line, posting a 35.7% success rate in the red zone, 125th nationally . The Texas offense will come into this one banged up and already struggling. Neither offense is built to win a shootout. Texas vs. Missouri prop: Texas team total Under 23.5 Texas has posted negative offensive EPA per play in five straight games , and Coleman and Wingo were healthy for most of that stretch. Field position makes it worse. Texas ranks 137th of 138 teams in EPA per play on its own half of the field, so drives that start deep rarely flip the field. Missouri's defense ranks 11th in havoc rate at 19.1%, while Texas allows havoc on 17.1% of its snaps, 105th nationally. With Goosby out at left tackle, I don't see that gap closing. Texas vs. Missouri combo Every leg runs through the same idea. Texas' offense was already the weak link before its top receivers got hurt, and Missouri can win a low-scoring game at home. The moneyline anchors it. If Texas can't move the ball past midfield, Missouri doesn't need a big day from its own offense to win, and both totals stay low. picks.blurb: Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas vs. Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL trade deadline grades Latest CFP rankings Tatum, Celtics rout Brown, Sixers NFL trade deadline tracker Vikings trade for Cousins Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas vs. Missouri Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 7 Texas and No. 18 Missouri have only met once on the football field since the Tigers left the Big 12 along side Texas A&M for the SEC. That meeting was the 2017 Texas Bowl. What should scare Longhorns fans is the 2026 version is tinkering on the edge of a disappointing bowl like that. Especially if they can't beat a team like Missouri. The Tigers are a good team. It's easy to see Missouri winning on Saturday. They're ranked just 11 spots below Texas in the College Football Playoff rankings and have the same record. And Mizzou has home field advantage. Then why is Texas a -3.5-point favorite. Because a fully functioning Texas team is better than Missouri. But this Texas team isn't fully functioning. First, the injuries are starting to pile up. It was announced this week that the Longhorns have lost running back Hollywood Smothers and tight end Nick Townsend for the rest of the season. All-American right tackle Trevor Goosby is also out for the year. And UT has been without All-American EDGE Colin Simmons for weeks. In addition to trying to plug the injury holes, Texas coach Steve Sarkisian must also continue to work on the offense. At times it looks great. But its not trustworthy. Will Muschamp's defense will need to stand tall for a third game in a row if the offense can't get it going. Tommy Bresee's Prediction Texas walks into this Missouri game needing the win to feel confident about their CFP chance heading into LSU. Missouri is a relative unknown, with losses to both Mississippi schools but a dominating win over Florida. Jamal Roberts and the run game leads the way, averaging just over 160 rushing yards/game. Austin Simmons has become a riser in this upcoming NFL Draft, flashing his elite arm talent every week. Texas was able to get a win over Tennessee earlier this season, but I don't see this as a task that's comparable. Missouri is capable of performing at a high level on both sides of the ball, especially the front seven defensively. It's difficult to imagine this Texas offense to trade punches with Missouri, especially on the road, so I'll take the Tigers to possibly end Texas' CFP hopes. Final Score: Texas 20, Missouri 23 Jamie Gatlin's Prediction The Longhorns will take on Missouri this Saturday in their latest SEC clash. The Tigers are off to an impressive 6-2 start and, like Texas, are 3-2 in conference play. Texas will need Arch Manning to be at his best and for the defense to shine. Last week, the Longhorns defense held Mississippi State to three points and 187 total yards. If the Longhorns can replicate that performance, another win could be on the horizon. This should be a game that Texas can win as they look to improve their playoff odds. Final Score: Texas 31, Missouri 13 Trey Luerssen's Prediction When this year's schedule came out, I thought the game against Mizzou might be the toughest to forecast. But it's even tougher now, because we're not sure which team will actually show up on either side of the ball. Both teams have had some big wins and some real clunkers. How much will Texas miss Smothers and Townsend? Can the defense slow down the Tigers offense? Which version of quarterback Arch Manning will show up in Columbia? For four games in a row, Texas has jumped out to an early lead and then coughed it up by the end of the third quarter. UT is 2-2 in that stretch. A coin flip. Twice the dam broke and twice it didn't. I think the defense will save the offense again. By Adam Spencer Published: Nov 6, 2026 · 11:41 AM EST The 6-2 Missouri Tigers host the 6-2 Texas Longhorns at Faurot Field on Saturday in what will almost certainly be a College Football Playoff elimination game. The Longhorns ride a 2-game winning streak into this pivotal road test, while the Tigers look to capitalize on the momentum of a dominant recent road victory. This conference showdown features 2 explosive offensive units—Missouri averages 31 points per game, narrowly edging out Texas's 30.8—led by capable signal-callers in Arch Manning and Austin Simmons. However, digging into the statistics reveals contrasts in how these squads operate. Texas boasts a lethal 93.3% conversion rate inside the 20-yard line, while Mizzou leans on offensive volume and ball security to overwhelm opponents. Win Probabilities: Texas vs. Missouri Kalshi currently favors the Texas Longhorns in this SEC road matchup, pricing them as the more likely winner. The market assigns Texas a 57% win probability against Missouri's 44%. This market lean toward Texas is notable given the Tigers' underlying statistical advantages. Missouri generates 424.6 total yards per game compared to Texas's 359.1 and boasts a +8 turnover differential with just 5 giveaways all year. Texas, conversely, has coughed it up 12 times to sit at a -3 differential. However, the market appears to weigh Texas's elite red-zone efficiency (93.3% conversion rate), fearsome pass rush (26 sacks), and superior brand of recent play more heavily than Missouri's between-the-20s dominance. Missouri's ability to sustain drives (42% on third down) and win the possession battle offers a path to an upset, but the Kalshi market sees the Longhorns as the side to back. Texas vs. Missouri Prediction and Expected Final Score We expect the Tigers to secure a critical conference victory by weaponizing their efficiency and ball security. Given the high-scoring nature of both offenses, a total-points expectation in the low-to-mid 60s is likely. Both teams consistently clear the 30-point threshold, pointing toward a potential shootout at Faurot. Ultimately, Missouri's superior yardage output and reliable ball security should be enough to edge out Texas in a tightly contested fourth quarter. Predicted Final Score: Missouri Tigers 34, Texas Longhorns 30 Arch Manning vs. Austin Simmons Comparison This matchup features a compelling quarterback duel between 2 capable passers pushing the ball down the field with impressive efficiency. Texas's Arch Manning and Missouri's Austin Simmons have both orchestrated 30-plus point offenses, but a granular look at their passing metrics exposes a massive disparity in turnover risk. Both quarterbacks thrive on vertical concepts, with Simmons averaging 8.1 yards per attempt compared to Manning's 8.0. Manning holds a slight edge in accuracy (64.8% completion rate against Simmons's 63.3%), but Simmons operates with higher volume, tallying 1,952 air yards to Manning's 1,727. The undeniable separator here is pocket discipline and decision-making. Simmons has been exceptionally careful, throwing just 2 interceptions on 240 attempts—a foundational piece of Missouri's elite turnover margin. Manning, on the other hand, has put the ball in harm's way too often, tossing 7 interceptions. While Manning's 15 touchdowns prove his playmaking upside, his propensity for mistakes could be fatal against an opportunistic Missouri defense. Texas vs. Missouri Head-to-Head History and Current Form A dive into the historical archives reveals a distinctly one-sided series, with Texas leading the all-time head-to-head 18-6 across 24 meetings. The Longhorns have overpowered the Tigers in 4 of their last 5 matchups, typically doing so in blowout fashion. The programs haven't shared a field in nearly a decade, last meeting in the 2017 Texas Bowl where Texas cruised to a 17-point neutral-site victory. Current Form: Texas Longhorns Despite a mid-October stumble against Florida (27-24), Texas brings steady momentum into Columbia following consecutive home wins over Ole Miss (34-27) and Mississippi State (31-3). The October 31 rout of the Bulldogs showcased the Longhorns' defensive prowess. Texas limited Mississippi State (without Kamario Taylor) to a paltry 187 total yards. The Longhorns amassed 280 total yards—220 passing, 60 rushing—and played clean, 1-turnover football. Current Form: Missouri Tigers Mizzou's recent trajectory mirrors Texas's mid-season resilience. After a lopsided 31-3 road loss to Ole Miss, the Tigers roared back on Halloween, dismantling the Arkansas Razorbacks 34-10 on the road. They generated 390 total yards of offense (211 rushing, 179 passing) while committing just 1 turnover. More importantly, the Tigers' defense wreaked havoc, forcing 4 Arkansas turnovers to win the possession battle decisively. Replicating that exact formula—establishing the run and taking the ball away—will be their blueprint to burying the Longhorns. home.blurb: Texas RB Hollywood Smothers Out for Rest of Season Texas Gets Devastating Hollywood Smothers Injury Update Ahead of Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Tatum, Celtics rout Brown, Sixers Story by Texas Longhorns On SI videos Texas Gets Devastating Hollywood Smothers Injury Update Ahead of Missouri Texas Longhorns running back Hollywood Smothers (2) warms up before a game against the Mississippi State Cougars at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Zach Dimmitt · Texas Longhorns On SI videos Thu, November 5, 2026 at 8:01 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Texas Longhorns have been no stranger to the injury bug this season, though this hasn't stopped the team from being firmly in the College Football Playoff race. Already without starting left tackle Trevor Goosby for the remainder of the season, the injury issues have piled up for Texas headed into Saturday's road matchup with the Missouri Tigers. Now, the Longhorns are receiving worst-case scenario news when it comes to starting running back Hollywood Smothers, who exited last week's game against Mississippi State with an apparent lower-body injury. Smothers will miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to a torn MCL in his knee, according to multiple reports. He started the year off as the team's starter after transferring in from NC State. In the second half against Mississippi State, Smothers took a hard hit to his lower body and sat on the turf holding his left knee. He was then helped off the field by trainers and was unable to put any weight on his left leg. Smothers finishes his 2026 season with 69 carries for 283 yards and two touchdowns along with 10 catches for 79 yards and another score. His pair of rushing touchdowns came in one of the biggest moments of Texas' season, as he had two scores in the fourth quarter against Ohio State, highlighted by the game-winning touchdown in the final minute to complete the comeback. The Longhorns have already gotten accustomed to life without Smothers this season. He previously dealt with ankle and shoulder injuries, forcing him to miss games against Tennessee and Ole Miss. Texas running back Raleek Brown now becomes the no-doubt starter moving forward for the Longhorns. So far this season, he's tallied 92 carries for 452 yards and five touchdowns along with 12 catches for 54 yard and another score. This was highlighted by an impressive performance in the win over Ole Miss when he had 23 carries for 157 yards. Behind him, Michael Terry III and Derrek Cooper will continue to receive an uptick in snaps. Terry has impressed and appears to have overtaken Cooper on the depth chart. It feels likely Terry will be Brown's backup moving forward. No. 7 Texas and No. 18 Missouri will kickoff from Columbia on Saturday at 11 a.m. CT. The Bruins are 8-0 this season and one of the best stories in the sport under first-year head coach Bob Chesney. Can Minnesota stop their momentum? Here are our staff writers' predictions. Tony Liebert: Minnesota 21, UCLA 14 P.J. Fleck has a track record of performing well as a home underdog, and he has a great chance to add to that narrative this week against UCLA. The Bruins haven't played on the road since sneaking past Oregon for their best win on Oct. 10. The only thing that scares me for the Gophers' chances this week is a hangover after last week's emotional loss to Indiana, but I expect Fleck's team to be ready to end UCLA's perfect season. Joe Nelson: Minnesota 21, UCLA 17 I don't want to say UCLA doesn't deserve to be ranked in the top 10, but who have they actually beaten to prove they're legit? Oregon without Dante Moore? Please. Every team gives the Ducks a run for their money this year. Wisconsin's a fraud; Purdue can't play defense; Michigan State, Nevada, Maryland, San Diego State and Cal all stink. As long as Minnesota doesn't get gashed on the ground, they're going to limit Ty Dieffenbach through the air. Dieffenbach can't move (kinda like Mr. Statue Drake Lindsey), and that's bad news for the Bruins, who will go home with an 8-1 record Will Ragatz: Minnesota 20, UCLA 17 Since getting embarrassed by Purdue, the Gophers have upset Iowa and come oh-so-close to doing the same to Indiana. They've done it by dragging those ranked teams into low-scoring slugfests. Can they do it to undefeated UCLA this week? I'm inclined to think they can. Outside of Oregon and maybe Wisconsin, the Bruins haven't exactly beaten anyone notable. Backup QB Ty Dieffenbach is still fairly inexperienced. And UCLA is coming to Minneapolis to play in 40-degree temps in a game that kicks off at 9 a.m. Pacific time. This will be another big win and field storm for P.J. Fleck. Jonathan Harrison: Minnesota 18, UCLA 15 On the road last week, the Gophers surprised everybody and took the defending champs to overtime. Despite an offense that can't seem to get going, Minnesota has hung around in most games. I think we'll see something similar with the Gophers' defense limiting a UCLA offense that is somehow averaging fewer passing yards than Minnesota this season. The Bruins have a top-15 run game, though, so Minnesota's defense will have its hands full there. This is going to be the question going forward: until proven otherwise, can the Gophers' offense do just enough to squeak out a win? I'm predicting that, with the home crowd behind them, that's the case on Saturday. Here are our picks from last week . The Bruins were No. 8 in the first round of College Football Playoff rankings, which doesn't matter. If they end up 10-2, as a Big Ten team, they're a mortal lock to get into the CFP. But at this point, they want a spot in the Big Ten Championship, and they're good enough to beat anyone left on the slate. Minnesota has proven it's almost good enough to beat anyone, losing a brutal 23-16 heartbreaker to Indiana last week. It beat Iowa and Michigan, but a weird 41-13 loss at Purdue is an issue for an at-large CFP spot. However, win out, and there's a shot at getting into the Big Ten title game. UCLA vs Minnesota: Quick Hits UCLA gets Illinois in the Rose Bowl next, then has to travel to Michigan, and finishes up down the road at USC. Minnesota goes to Penn State next week, hosts Northwestern, and close with the Paul Bunyan Axe game at Wisconsin. The two programs have only faced each other four times, with Minnesota winning the last meeting 21-17 in 2024. The Gophers are 3-1, starting with a 21-3 win in the 19162 Rose Bowl. How To Watch UCLA vs Minnesota Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis, MN – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why UCLA Will Win Run, run, and keep running. There's no real mystery to what UCLA does. It blasts away, with the ground game, gets just enough from the passing game to get by, and then it relies on the defense to take care of everything else. It starts with third down stops. Only Nebraska – at least before the loss to Illinois – is better at defensively on third downs than the Bruins. That allows UCLA to dominate the time of possession battle, the rested defense forces a ton of takeaways, the offense capitalizes … repeat. However … Why Minnesota Will Win UCLA runs well, Minnesota doesn't. Minnesota can throw well, UCLA doesn't. Other than that, these two do almost all of the same things. You want third down defense? Minnesota is sixth in the nation, allowing teams to convert just 28% of their chances. Time of possession? The Gophers aren't as good as UCLA, but they're fine, usually keeping the ball for close to 32 minutes per game. And then there are the takeaways – Minnesota is good at that, too. UCLA vs Minnesota Prediction, Betting Lines The whole Big Noon Kickoff aspect to this is a problem for UCLA. The Bruins have to be ready to rumble at 9:00 am Los Angeles time. And then there's the other issue. When the ball gets kicked off in Minneapolis, it will be around 71 degrees in LA. The temperature should hover around 40 degrees and feel more like 32ish for the entire game in Huntington Bank. UCLA will be pushed and tested, and Minnesota will take advantage of that early, but the score will be kept low throughout, and the Bruins will still be alive in the second half, when the ground game starts to take over. It'll be another tremendously entertaining Minnesota game to kick off a whale of a Saturday. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 5 Alabama is out to defend its College Football Playoff ranking, while No. 14 LSU seeks to remain in the hunt Getty Images One of the best modern-day rivalries in college football headlines on Saturday when No. 5 Alabama and No. 14 LSU meet in Baton Rouge for the 91st meeting in the series. The Crimson Tide hold a 58-27-5 advantage overall, but it's the 13-2 record in the past 15 meetings that has given them the upper hand in a battle between programs that would otherwise be considered peers. This is, after all, set to be the 25th time that both schools are inside the top 15 of the AP Top 25 poll and with Alabama's recent crowning as a top-five team in the College Football Playoff rankings, there's even more ranked-on-ranked intrigue. LSU is hoping that the home field advantage of Death Valley can play a role in the game, as the Tigers are 32-3 in their last 35 home games in Tiger Stadium. Speaking of streaks, the game also presents LSU coach Lane Kiffin with a chance to finally defeat Alabama as a head coach. The former Crimson Tide offensive coordinator lost to Nick Saban once as Tennessee's head coach in 2009, then four times between 2020-23 as Ole Miss ' head coach, when they were SEC West division rivals. That 0-5 record against the Crimson Tide, paired with LSU's recent struggles in the series, provides plenty of extra motivation for the home team looking to roar back into the playoff race. Where to watch Alabama vs. LSU live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Tiger Stadium -- Baton Rouge, Louisiana TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Alabama vs. LSU: Need to know Alabama's injury report will be an X-factor: There will be key updates throughout the week, perhaps all the way up to warm-ups, that will determine the health of the Crimson Tide and their ability to perform to the expectations of their top-five rating. Starting center Racin Delgatty has missed multiple games while dealing with injury, and his absence has been noticeable on an offensive line that has cooled off since putting up 49+ points in consecutive wins against Florida State , South Carolina and Mississippi State . The Crimson Tide have failed to record 70+ rushing yards as a team in each of their last two games and allowed 21 sacks in SEC play, which ranks 14th among 16 teams in the league. Alabama will also be looking for updates from star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and cornerback Zabien Brown , adding to the unknowns for how the Tide will stack up against LSU. LSU passing attack rounding into form : No one in the SEC had a more productive passing attack in the month of October than LSU, which averaged 339.5 passing yards across all four games last month. The Tigers went 3-1 across those games, only losing to top-10 Kentucky by one point in Lexington on a walk-off two-point try. LSU now leads the SEC and ranks tied for 7th nationally on the season, averaging 318.0 passing yards per game, and the improvements have come with both Sam Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris as a go-to receiver. A transfer from Hawaii , Harris played three whole games before scoring his first touchdown of the season but has exploded ever since with seven touchdown catches across the last five games. That includes four multiple-touchdown games and a yards-per-reception average (17.6) that ranks 4th among all SEC pass catchers. Kalen DeBoer set up in some favorable situational spots : When Alabama hired Kalen DeBoer away from Washington to take over in Tuscaloosa after Nick Saban's retirement, his track record as a big-time, high-leverage coach met the demands of the job. Since Alabama is almost always playing in high-pressure games against quality opponents, the school needed to know that Saban's successor would be ready for those moments. Currently, DeBoer is 21-8 against AP-ranked teams as a head coach, which is the fourth-best record in AP poll history with a minimum of 20 games coached (.724 winning percentage). His company on that list, for those unaware, is one spot behind Urban Meyer (.746) and one spot ahead of Kirby Smart (.710). DeBoer has also won eight straight games after a bye, with the last defeat in this spot coming in 2020 as the head coach of Fresno State . Alabama vs. LSU prediction, picks While the combination of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell provides the potential for plenty of points, this game could end up being decided by both defenses. Alabama's offensive injuries have clearly limited their ability to execute on schedule, and LSU's defense represents the best test they've faced since the loss at Tennessee. In the same manner, LSU's pass attack could set them up for some of the turnovers that have powered Alabama's excellence this season (+7 turnover margin is tied for 11th nationally) and prevent touchdowns even after successful drives. All in all, it points to a lower-scoring classic, where I'll favor the home team to make big plays late. Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB With three losses on the season, the LSU Tigers find themselves in a rough spot in an attempt to make the College Football Playoff this season. After being dismantled at home by the Alabama Crimson Tide , reaching the coveted post-season seems unlikely in year one of the Lane Kiffin era, and there is another top-ranked team waiting just around the corner for the Tigers. Having already fallen in the AP Pol l, to nearly on the outside looking in, where will the Tigers find themselves in the second College Football Playoff rankings ? With two losses already on the year heading into the first set of College Football Playoff rankings, the Tigers' room for error was minimal, and their ranking reflected that, coming in at No. 14. A win over the Crimson Tide would have put the Tigers in a comfortable position for the rest of the year, especially given the rest of the schedule remaining. Instead, with three losses, their ranking will plummet during the second release. Despite the loss, the Tigers shouldn't fall out of the top 25, as the committee has proven it won't shy away from ranking three-loss teams. Three were ranked last week: the South Carolina Gamecocks, the Oregon Ducks, and the Florida Gators. The Tigers should, at a minimum, replace the Gators, who suffered a fourth loss of the season this past weekend. The Missouri Tigers, who were also ranked and lost a third game of the season, should fall, but they also played a closer game against the top-ranked Texas Longhorns. The Ohio State Buckeyes will plummet as well, and they entered the weekend ranked higher than the Tigers. Considering those two teams, and the inclusion of potentially the New Mexico Lobos, who continue to find ways to win this season, there are a handful of teams fighting for fewer spots than available. With that said, the Tigers, just based on team talent alone, and every win being dominant so far this year, should be around No. 22-25, probably right at No. 24, providing another ranked SEC matchup this weekend against the Texas Longhorns. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs LSU: LSU -5.5 The last time LSU won the Saban Bowl, Nick Saban was Alabama's head coach and Lane Kiffin was still beloved at Ole Miss . That will change Saturday when Kiffin's surging Tigers take advantage of a Crimson Tide team that's looked like a far cry from its No. 5 College Football Playoff ranking. With LSU's defensive ferocity and Alabama's offensive struggles, I like the Tigers to cover up to -6.5 at home against the Tide. Not only has LSU's defense been wrecking opponents, but the Tigers' offense has been on fire too, with Sam Leavitt fourth nationally in QBR (85.3) and 12th in adjusted completion percentage (79.5%). Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris (480 receiving yards and seven TDs in his last four SEC games) are a problem for an Alabama defense that's ranked 78th in pass success rate (44.3%). Alabama vs LSU Over/Under pick: Under 52.5 This game isn't one of the must-watch games in my college football Top 25 predictions this week because I'm expecting offensive fireworks; it's because of the talent on these defenses. LSU's defense is especially loaded, and with Alabama's struggles against quality defenses, I would play the Under at 51.5 or better. The Tigers are second nationally in sacks (34) , and Keelon Russell hasn't managed pressure well. He's been sacked the ninth-most in the country (22) and has a 20.4% pressure-to-sack rate. If those two don't play, Alabama will struggle to score even 20 points. The Crimson Tide don't have consistent playmakers outside of Coleman-Williams, and LSU's defense brings the heat, ranking fourth nationally in havoc rate (22.2%) .
