If Alabama gets off to another slow start and trails LSU, the Tigers' defense will pin their ears back and go to work. LSU ranks eighth nationally in pass success rate on defense (36%) and has one of the most lethal pass rush duos in the country, Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross (58 combined pressures and 13.5 sacks). Each team is coming off a bye week, giving them more rest and time to prepare for this huge game. With SEC schedule changes coming, this matchup will be the last one played between the two teams on a yearly basis. This could add more emphasis for both sides to want to come away with the win. With this rivalry game kicking off in a few days, the Crimson Tide aren't being favored to come away with the win on the road. The Crimson Tide (6-2, 4-2 SEC) is heading to Baton Rouge, Louisiana with its back against the wall, heading into a matchup against LSU (6-2, 3-2 SEC) with two losses and, seemingly, not much room for error. Alabama has won three straight against LSU, each of which came by double-digits. Alabama's last loss to the Tigers came in 2022 at Tiger Stadium, the Crimson Tide's only loss in its last seven road trips to Baton Rouge. No. 9 Alabama will face No. 15 LSU at 2:30 p.m. CT Saturday, Nov. 7 on ABC. Can Alabama continue to save its 2026 season with a win at LSU? Here are the top storylines and an Alabama vs. LSU score prediction. Alabama vs LSU scouting report Here are the biggest storylines going into Alabama vs. LSU: Can Keelon Russell find his magic in an SEC road game? Keelon Russell's production has taken a significant dip on the road. His passing offense average dips by 40 yards paired a problematic ratio of four passing touchdowns to four interceptions. LSU has one of the better pass defenses in the SEC, tied with Tennessee with allowing the fewest passing touchdowns in the conference along with 172.75 passing yards per game and a 60% completion rate. Can Russell find a way to be himself despite everything seemingly stacked against him? Will Alabama force LSU QB Sam Leavitt to make mistakes? LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt does make mistakes. In eight games, Leavitt has an SEC-high eight interceptions. He had at least one in each of his first six games of 2026. He hasn't thrown one in his last two games against Auburn and Mississippi State: the bottom two pass defenses in the SEC. Alabama may allow 222.38 passing yards per game, but the Crimson Tide is tied for the conference lead with 12 interceptions. Can Alabama's ball-hawk secondary exploit Leavitt and the LSU passing attack? Can Alabama run the ball against LSU? Alabama has 122 rushing yards combined in its past two games against Tennessee and Texas A&M: 29 yards below its per-game average which is already 12th best in the SEC. And Alabama is tasked with facing the seventh-best run defense nationally and the best run defense in the SEC in an LSU front that allows just over 85 yards per game and 2.69 yards per rush. Can Alabama's running back room provide any semblance of downhill consistency against the Tigers? away.headline: Josh Ford set to miss rest of Alabama football season, per reports
away.blurb: “Josh suffered an injury, and it can be season-ending,” DeBoer said. “I mean, the guy’s so tough, I know he’s probably right now, he’s trying to figure out how he’s still gonna play this year. It’s just who he is. His impact has been really key for our football team in a lot of ways. Just a guy that’s a uniter. You’ve got uniters and dividers, I think, and he’s a uniter of our football team. He’s a leader.” Alabama tight end Josh Ford is set to miss the remainder of the season with a knee injury, Kalen DeBoer confirmed on Monday. Ford sustained a torn ACL late in the Crimson Tide’s 31-13 victory over LSU this past Saturday, according to the school’s NIL entity. He had caught a touchdown pass earlier in the game. Ford transferred to the Crimson Tide ahead of the 2026 season from Oklahoma State. Primarily a blocking tight end who was a tone setter, Ford also caught five passes for 41 yards and two touchdowns. CBS Sports was first to report the news. Ford already was playing through a broken bone in his arm, sustained during the Oct. 3 win over Mississippi State in Starkville. He had surgery shortly thereafter and played the following week vs. Georgia with a cast on his arm. Without Ford at tight end, Alabama still has Kaleb Edwards, Marshall Pritchett, Jay Lindsey and Danny Lewis. Pritchett and Edwards have been bigger targets in the passing game, but they and others will have to step up with Ford not able to help block. “Danny Lewis, kind of starts with him,” Alabama offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb said. “He’s your next pure inline Y or blocker ... Kaleb is obviously our guy. He’s our starting Y. I think you know I can’t say enough good about 81, and I was not surprised that he played as well as he did. I know he had the holding call on the big run that got called back, but he played a whale of a football game. And I think he’s one of the five or six tight ends in the country that are that 6-5 260-pound, true 50-50 player that can block and catch, and you know you don’t give any tells away when he’s on the field because he can do both. Think the world of Kaleb. Probably going to put a little bit more on his plate, and then, like I said, Danny Lewis is a guy that will step up certainly. And Jay Lindsey will have probably more of an expanded role as well.” The Crimson Tide (7-2, 5-2 SEC) plays at Vanderbilt on Saturday. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit al.com. home.blurb: Alabama (7-2, 5-2) played like its season depended on it, jumping out to a first-half lead and overpowering the Tigers in their own home for a 31-13 victory. Freshman quarterback Kaelon Russell put on a show, throwing for 206 yards and three touchdowns, picking LSU’s defense apart when it matter most. Despite being outgained in total yards of offense, the Crimson Tide made the most of every red zone trip they had, while the same couldn’t be said for Lane Kiffin and his Tigers. LSU ended the game going 2 out of 4 in its red zone visits, with both of those red zone trips ending in field goals instead of touchdowns. After a 32-yard punt return from Coleman-Williams, Russell only needed one play to extend Alabama's lead in the fourth quarter. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 12 Ohio State hosts No. 23 Oregon in a pivotal game in the Big Ten and CFP race Getty Images Week 10 of the college football season has been highlighted since the schedule was released, with No. 23 Oregon's trip to face No. 12 Ohio State among the headliners. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling. The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Oregon live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Ohio Stadium -- Columbus, Ohio TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com , CBS Sports App Streaming on Paramount+ Premium Ohio State vs. Oregon: Need to know Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana , it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore ). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road. Ohio State vs. Oregon prediction, picks The Ducks have to pick up where they left off offensively to have a chance here, and they should push the tempo a bit and try to stretch things out in the air. Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. Ohio State (6-2, 4-1 Big Ten) is back in Columbus in a must-win spot against the Oregon Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) for both their conference title and playoff lives. What was thought to be a matchup of national title-contending heavyweights is far different, and only one can remain near the top of a crowded league. Find out whether our On SI crew is backing the Buckeyes as kickoff and the game are underway. Now they find themselves with their back against the wall, likely needing to run the table to go back to Indianapolis for the second straight season. Before they can focus on that, however, they need to knock off Oregon, which still has a chance to be one-half of the championship game if things break the Ducks’ way despite three losses (including an outright upset against Illinois in late October). Last week, Oregon overcame a 14-point deficit to beat Northwestern and protect home-field advantage. This week, Ohio State can’t fall into a similar trap by getting comfortable with an early lead. There could be a chaotic finish in this one, and if Ohio State has the ball last, its chances to win and remain prevalent in the Big Ten title race will be very much alive. But only time will tell. Rafael Zamorano: Ohio State 23, Oregon 21 It might not be a do-or-die moment yet for Ohio State, currently ranked 12th in the nation with four games left on the schedule, but it sure feels like one. And, as it’s been for most of the year, expect Jeremiah Smith to receive most of the targets on offense -- although it seems pretty clear that the Buckeyes could benefit from spreading the ball around a little more to keep defenses honest. Having said that, dropping a third regular-season game this Saturday against Oregon would no doubt shrink the Buckeyes’ playoff chances dramatically Luckily for Ohio State, Oregon’s season hasn’t turned out as expected either, after starting off as the No. 2-ranked team in the land, one spot behind the Buckeyes. On paper, Oregon might still be the most formidable opponent left on the season calendar, but these aren’t the same Ducks widely projected to be competing for a Natty just a couple of months ago. Ohio State will need to show a ton of improvement in the passing game, especially when it comes to getting true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey into a rhythm. I see the Buckeyes getting back to the win column in a tight one. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 28, Oregon 24 "Desperate Measures” would be the title of this game if it were a movie. Ohio State sits at 6-2, Oregon at 5-3, and it is a legitimate point to make that the loser of this game could be on the outside looking in at The College Football Playoff. While people are understandably concerned about the play of Luke Fahey, Ohio State’s loss at USC last week was more on the defensive side of the ball, and Oregon has many talented players who should have Ohio State defensive coordinator Matt Patricia burning the midnight oil in preparation this week. If there is a bright spot, Oregon QB Dylan Raiola has shown a tendency to turn the ball over, so perhaps Coach Patricia will turn up the pressure to force some mistakes. Field position will be at a premium. Brace yourselves, Ohio State fans — Oregon has even more talent on the defensive line than USC does, so it will be imperative that Fahey gets the ball out quickly, or at least runs for positive yardage when and if the pocket breaks down. Kicking field goals may be crucial in this one, even though Ohio State understandably wants touchdowns. Here's hoping that Ohio State has been working on their red zone woes. I believe it will be a back-and-forth, and this is the type of game that feels like whichever team has the ball last will have the opportunity to win it in the final moments. Give me Ohio State in a nail-biter. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 20, USC 17 Coming into the 2026 college football season, this was penciled early on as one of the most impactful games of the season, with both teams expected to be in the top 10, with heavy Big Ten implications on the line. Oh, how things can change quickly in a short two months. Oregon is basically out of the playoff picture, while Ohio State’s chances are hanging on by a thread. This still sets the stage for a dramatic 3:30 kickoff this Saturday in Columbus, with the Buckeyes needing to answer a lot of questions after a 30-18 loss at USC last week. The defense should be stronger for Ohio State in this matchup, cleaning up mistakes that cost them against the Trojans and causing turnovers against an inconsistent Oregon offense. Yet, playmakers Evan Stewart and Dakorien Moore can turn a big play out of nowhere, and the Buckeyes have shown they are susceptible to it. Oregon is able to cash in on a few big plays, with their defense making this game a sweat. Yet, the budding run game and a clean game from freshman quarterback Luke Fahey does just enough for Ohio State to escape this game with a win, and playoff hopes that stay alive heading into their final three games of the season. In the long history of this rivalry, there's a good case that this is the biggest game ever. In his first year on the job, Will Stein has led Kentucky to a 7-1 start and a great shot at reaching the College Football Playoff with just four games remaining. His major transfer portal additions -- particularly quarterback Kenny Minchey and the offensive line -- clicked almost immediately. To this point, the Wildcats have passed all but one test they've faced, but the level of difficulty rises this weekend. Kentucky must continue to play clean football if it wants to come away with a win in Knoxville. Tennessee had two weeks to wallow in the "what if" after its three-point loss to South Carolina , but the team has to get back in the saddle this weekend. The Volunteers have the chance to pick up their second top-10 win of the season, which would really boost their CFP rankings. There's no doubt that the Vols have a playoff-caliber defense and running game, but can Josh Heupel fix the passing attack? Tennessee must improve there to reach its ceiling. Here is everything you need to know about this top-15 rivalry matchup in Knoxville. Tennessee vs. Kentucky: Need to know Rare ranked matchup: These teams have met well over 100 times, but this is just the fourth ranked matchup in history. Most recently, Tennessee and Kentucky played a top-25 matchup in 2022, with the Volunteers winning in a blowout. Prior to that, the only times the Vols and Wildcats were ranked simultaneously were in 1950 and 1951. That means there's a very good case for this matchup to be the biggest in the history of this rivalry. Games with stakes in this series usually go the way of Tennessee, but can Stein turn the tables on Saturday night? Kentucky not in the giving spirit: The holidays are approaching quickly, but Kentucky has not been feeling very generous. One of the driving factors behind the Wildcats' success is their incredible plus-13 turnover margin. That ranks first in the SEC and fourth in the entire country. For the first time since 2013, Kentucky has avoided turning the ball over in three consecutive games. If any team can end that streak, it's probably Tennessee, which has a great defense and has forced 14 turnovers in eight games. The Vols just have to protect the ball on offense. Heavy dose of DeSean Bishop : Kentucky defensive coordinator Jay Bateman probably doesn't need my advice, but I would suggest he lock in on Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop. He's been the engine of the Vols offense, and his 957 rushing yards rank sixth in the country. His 12 rushing touchdowns are tied for ninth. Over the last four games, Bishop has averaged 29 carries and 159 yards. If the Wildcats can contain Bishop and force Tennessee to throw the ball, that could be a recipe for success, but only one team has effectively shut Bishop down to this point. Kentucky's offense has been incredibly efficient, and it will pose a real challenge to the Tennessee defense. Pictured: Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop Ryan Minion · Action Network Sat, November 7, 2026 at 9:58 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kentucky Wildcats take on the Tennessee Volunteers in Knoxville, Tennessee, on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff is set for 6:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Despite entering Saturday's Week 10 clash with a 7-1 overall record on the season, Kentucky remains a 6.5-point road underdog with a +188 price tag to pull off the outright upset. Tennessee is favored by 5.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -220. Kentucky is a 5.5-point underdog with a moneyline of +184. The total is set at 49.5 points (-110 / -110). Here's my Kentucky vs. Tennessee prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 7. Kentucky vs. Tennessee Pick: Tennessee ML (-225) My Tennessee vs. Kentucky best bet is on the Volunteers to win outright. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page , and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Kentucky vs Tennessee Odds, Betting Line, Point Spread Kentucky vs Tennessee Spread : Kentucky +6, Tennessee -6 Kentucky vs Tennessee Over/Under : 49.5 Total Points Kentucky vs Tennessee Moneyline : Kentucky ML +170, Tennessee ML -205 In one of the bigger surprises of this college football season, the Wildcats have emerged as one of the best teams in the entire country in head coach Will Stein's first year at the helm. Kentucky senior QB Kenny Minchey has been phenomenal in his first season in Lexington after spending three years at Notre Dame and throwing the ball only 30 times there. Minchey has thrown for 1755 yards and 14 touchdowns over the Wildcats' first eight games this season with just one turnover. Freshman WR Kenny Darby has been Minchey's favorite target with over 500 yards and three touchdowns. Stein's rushing attack has been effective too, with senior tailback CJ Baxter rushing for nearly 500 yards and eight touchdowns. The Wildcat offense is averaging just shy of 33 points per game this season, but will get its most difficult test on Saturday against an elite Tennessee pass rush. Kentucky's defense has thrived under defensive coordinator Jay Bateman, who has built an aggressive, havoc -creating unit that has fared well against some elite SEC offenses this season. The Wildcats lead the SEC in interceptions and pass breakups, boasting an elite secondary led by veteran safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell. While its front seven struggled early this season, Kentucky has improved drastically in the trenches over the course of the season. The 8th-ranked Wildcats are in a great spot to potentially qualify for the playoffs, but still must face several difficult conference opponents, starting with the Vols in Week 10. The 16th-ranked Volunteers put their postseason hopes on the line as Josh Heupel's bunch looks to evade a third loss this season that would very likely ruin their playoff resume. After a very promising 6-1 start to the season despite an ongoing QB battle between George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon , Tennessee was defeated on the road at South Carolina this past weekend for the Vols' second loss of the year. Now they face a must-win game, with lingering questions about whether Heupel will stick with MacIntyre under center or return to top-ranked freshman QB Brandon. Regardless, betting markets have made their stance quite clear, with Tennessee currently listed as a near-touchdown favorite despite the Wildcats' breakout 7-1 campaign. While WR Mike Matthews has recorded over 500 receiving yards this season, Tennessee has relied far more on its rushing attack, with tailback DeSean Bishop rushing for 957 yards and 11 touchdowns, ranking sixth and ninth in all of college football, respectively. However, the Vols' defense has thrived all year, particularly at home, where it allows SEC opponents the third-fewest PPG in the conference (16.25). Jim Knowles was brought in as defensive coordinator this past offseason after serving in the same capacity for Penn State , and has significantly improved a unit that fell to 81st in the country in EPA (Expected Points Added) last season. Tennessee's defense boasts an elite linebacker corps ranked in the top 10 nationally, featuring Edwin Spillman, Amare Campbell, Arion Carter, and Jeremiah Telander. While the Vols' defense has carried this team for most of the season, especially at home in Knoxville, their offense will need to show up in this matchup, given how impressive Michey has been at avoiding turnovers. I expect this to be one of the best matchups in an absolutely loaded Week 10 slate. While I have been very impressed with the Wildcats offense and a much-improved defensive unit, I expect the atmosphere to be quite chaotic given how difficult it is for SEC foes to escape Neyland Stadium in Knoxville with an outright victory. The Vols boast an extremely dominant pass rush that should give Kentucky's offensive line fits considering how much that unit has struggled to contain elite edge pressure. That said, I feel betting markets are giving Tennessee a tad too much credit given their fragile situation at QB. In what I expect to be a pretty closely contested matchup, I'm going with the Volunteers moneyline. I got it at -210 earlier this week as soon as the line opened, and while I typically don't lay that much juice on a moneyline, especially considering the volatility of betting college football, I have confidence Tennessee gets the outright win, but laying close to a touchdown versus a red-hot Wildcat bunch is far from ideal. Though Tennessee's moneyline has since crept up to -230, I still don't mind playing the Vols at that number. picks.blurb: Tennessee football vs Kentucky picks: Vols don't lose to Wildcats in Knoxville, right? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL trade deadline grades Latest CFP rankings Tatum, Celtics rout Brown, Sixers NFL trade deadline tracker Vikings trade for Cousins Knoxville News Sentinel · The Tennessean Sat, November 7, 2026 at 10:06 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Tennessee football opens a November to either remember or forget with a top-15 matchup against Kentucky on Nov. 7 at Neyland Stadium The Vols (6-2, 3-2 SEC) lost at South Carolina two weeks ago on a last-second field goal, earning a second SEC loss before the final month of the season. Kentucky (7-1, 5-1) is also coming off of an open date and has a clear path to the SEC Championship Game and the CFP. First-year coach Will Stein has molded his roster into a team that limits its mistakes and maximizes other teams' turnovers. UK has beaten Tennessee in Knoxville once since 1984, the 2020 win in front of a COVID-limited crowd at Neyland. Here are Knox News' staff predictions for Tennessee-Kentucky: Tennessee-Kentucky expert predictions Adam Sparks, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 28, Kentucky 24 The Vols can certainly beat themselves against the most disciplined team in the SEC. Kentucky leads the league in turnover margin and fewest penalties. But UT can take control of this game by winning the line of scrimmage. That means DeSean Bishop earns bruising yards and UT's defensive line collapses the pocket around Kenny Minchey. Give Tennessee the edge because of the overwhelming atmosphere of Neyland Stadium in a night game in dark mode. Emmett Siegel, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 24, Kentucky 20 The Vols still have to find something in their passing game , which is statistically the worst in the SEC. Even if that doesn't come to fruition, though, Tennessee's rushing attack and defense have been good enough to beat the toughest teams on its schedule. Perhaps the open week helped Tennessee clean up some of last game's mistakes before playing a team that doesn't make many. Playing at home could push it over the top. Cora Hall, UT beat reporter: Kentucky 27, Tennessee 24 Both teams are had a week off and are rested going into this matchup, and the Wildcats have proven they can will their way to a win when it matters. The Vols will get close, but they've been too inconsistent to bet on a win here. Stephen Thompson, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 17, Kentucky 13 I've surrendered to the idea that George MacIntyre is who he is, at least for now. But Tennessee's defense is as good as any in the country and the Neyland effect will be a difference maker in another ugly, but tight win for the Vols. Wynton Jackson, sports reporter: Tennessee 26, Kentucky 21 The Vols likely need to be perfect throughout the rest of the season to reach the College Football Playoff. Coming off the bye, that road starts with an unexpected matchup against No. 7 Kentucky. The Wildcats have solid wins, but a trip to Neyland with a national spotlight brings heightened pressure. John Adams, columnist: Tennessee 27, Kentucky 20 The Wildcats have a better record and a higher national ranking than the Vols. Moreover, Kentucky is clearly headed in the right direction under first-year coach Will Stein. But history tells us that Tennessee is always the wrong direction for Kentucky football, which has lost 38 of the previous 41 games in the series. Gentry Estes, Tennessean columnist: Tennessee 23, Kentucky 14 Props to the Wildcats on a great season, but it just feels like they are due for a letdown in a tough rivalry road game. Neyland should be jumping for this one. This article originally appeared on Knoxville News Sentinel: Tennessee football vs Kentucky picks: Vols don't lose to Wildcats in Knoxville, right?

picks.blurb: Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL trade deadline grades Latest CFP rankings Tatum, Celtics rout Brown, Sixers NFL trade deadline tracker Vikings trade for Cousins Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to a hostile Neyland Stadium to take on the Tennessee Volunteers at 6:15 P.M. ET on Saturday night. This is a massive game with a lot at stake for both teams, the Wildcats are undefeated on the road this season and they will try to continue that streak in this game. We laid out the path to victory for Kentucky and the key areas they need to win to improve to 8-1 on the season. It is time to give some final thoughts on the matchup and give a game prediction. As I stated earlier in the week on my Tennessee defense preview , but I truly think this game comes down to Will Stein's offense versus Jim Knowles' defense. They have met three times and Coach Stein has gotten the best of Knowles in two of those three meetings. Kentucky has to continue to play efficient on offense and play clean. I think they have a great opportunity to methodically move the football down the field as they have all season against this defense. This game starts and ends in the trenches, on both sides of the football. Tennessee's defensive line is the strength of their team, but Kentucky's offensive line is playing better than any offensive line in the country. They have to stabilize defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam, who has been wrecking offensive gameplans all season long. A key matchup to watch is Kentucky center Coleton Price against Gilliam, Price has been one of the best centers in the country and he will have his hands full in this game. Kentucky has to win this game on the line of scrimmage, and I have confidence in the Wildcats offensive line to gain the edge in that matchup. Tennessee's offensive line has been above average as run blockers, but they do struggle in pass protection. Kentucky forcing Tennessee into a dropback heavy game script could be critical, but they have to stop the run in order to do that. Kentucky's defensive line has gotten consistent pressure all season, and I am very intrigued to see how this defensive line gets after a pocket passer like George MacIntyre because they have faced a mobile quarterback in every game this season. Kentucky has to win the line of scrimmage, and this is the best offensive line the Vols have faced this season. I think the Wildcats defensive line has been underrated this year, and they can make a statement on Saturday. The run defense has improved tremendously in the month of October, and slowing down the Vols heavy rushing attack is crucial. If they can force Tennessee into a heavy dropback game, Kentucky will be able to create turnovers like they have all season. Truthfully, I believe the biggest advantage is Kentucky's coaching staff getting two weeks to prepare for this football game. Tennessee is coming off the bye week as well, but Josh Heupel and Jim Knowles are going to do what they do. Kentucky's coaching staff has added plenty of wrinkles week-to-week, so I can only imagine what they will have in store with two weeks to prepare. This is an advantage for Kentucky, particularly on the offensive side of the football. We all know this history of this series, it has not been kind to Kentucky. However, this is a different era of college football and Kentucky football. If you remove the history and helmet logos, I think Kentucky has the advantage at quarterback and offensive line as well as a hotshot head coach that has done an unthinkable turnaround in year one for this program. It will be a close game in the fourth quarter, and how could you not trust Will Stein and Kenny Minchey under those circumstances. Prediction: Kentucky 24, Tennessee 20 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction

picks.blurb: Colin Cowherd Predicts National Championship Rematch After Notre Dame Win Over Miami Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Fox Sports host Colin Cowherd is sticking with Notre Dame and Miami as his national championship pairing after the Fighting Irish handed the top-ranked Hurricanes their first loss of the season, 31-24, Saturday night in South Bend. “Nothing I saw last night changes that opinion ,” Cowherd wrote on X on Sunday morning, adding that he said before the season the two programs “would meet for the natty” and that “only Georgia is close.” Why is Cowherd still riding with Notre Dame? Fans are seen on the field after Notre Dame Fighting Irish defeated the Miami Hurricanes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cowherd backed the Irish before they played a snap. “I picked Notre Dame to win the whole thing. They’re going to be my national champion ,” he said in late August. Cowherd backed the Irish before they played a snap. “I picked Notre Dame to win the whole thing. They’re going to be my national champion ,” he said in late August. Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr held up his end of that pick Saturday, completing 29 of 40 passes for 319 yards and three touchdowns. He hit Micah Gilbert for two scores and Jordan Faison for another as the Irish built a 24-3 lead early in the third quarter. Miami pulled within a touchdown, but Notre Dame safety Luke Talich intercepted Miami quarterback Darian Mensah late in the third quarter and later broke up a potential tying touchdown pass to tight end Elija Lofton. The win mattered most for an Irish team that entered with the No. 11 College Football Playoff ranking that surprised ESPN’s Kirk Herbstreit. Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman called it “ as special of a moment , as special of an outcome that I’ve been a part of since I’ve been the head coach here.” The Irish close the regular season against Boston College, SMU and Syracuse. Malachi Toney and a Miami rematch Miami (FL) Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney (1) celebrates with tight end Gavin Mueller (87) after scoring a touchdown | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cowherd attached one condition to his title game pick. “I would take the Canes in a rematch if Malachi Toney plays,” he wrote. Cowherd attached one condition to his title game pick. “I would take the Canes in a rematch if Malachi Toney plays,” he wrote. Miami wide receiver Malachi Toney suffered a high-ankle sprain in practice Wednesday and had tightrope surgery Thursday. The sophomore led the ACC with 73 catches, 1,027 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns through eight games, and CBS Sports reported he’s expected to miss four to six weeks . That timeline could put Toney back for the ACC Championship Game on Dec. 5 and keeps him on track for the playoff. His absence showed in a first half that ended with Miami trailing 17-3. Mensah then threw three second-half touchdown passes, two of them to Duke transfer Cooper Barkate. Miami finishes the regular season with home games against Duke, Virginia Tech and Boston College. Georgia rolls Ole Miss in Oxford Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart reacts during the second half against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The second-ranked Bulldogs backed up Cowherd’s lone exception Saturday, routing Ole Miss 42-7 as Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton threw four touchdown passes and ran for another. The second-ranked Bulldogs backed up Cowherd’s lone exception Saturday, routing Ole Miss 42-7 as Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton threw four touchdown passes and ran for another. Georgia led 28-0 at halftime, rushed for 295 yards and snapped Ole Miss’ 16-game home winning streak . The win was Georgia head coach Kirby Smart’s first at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, and it came days after former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer named Georgia the best team in college football . The selection committee releases its second College Football Playoff rankings Tuesday at approximately 9 p.m. ET on ESPN, and Georgia has a strong case to replace Miami at No. 1. My Miami vs. Notre Dame prediction and college football picks back Darian Mensah to keep things close without his top target, Malachi Toney. The Fighting Irish are 7.5-point home favorites as Miami visits Notre Dame Stadium in Notre Dame, Ind., on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC, with College GameDay also in town. Miami vs Notre Dame predictions for Week 10 ⭐Spread prediction Over/Under prediction Prop prediction Miami TT Over 23.5 TOP PICK Who will win Miami vs Notre Dame today: Miami +7.5 The news that Malachi Toney was injured in practice this week and won't play against Notre Dame has dominated headlines and shifted the Fighting Irish from 5.5-point favorites to 7.5-point favorites. But even without Toney, I like Miami to cover +6.5 or better on the road. Darian Mensah is among the Heisman Trophy favorites for a reason; he leads the country in QBR (90.3) and adjusted completion percentage (86.2%). He also has one of the best running back duos in college football and a No. 2 wide receiver in Cooper Barkate , whom he trusts immensely. Mensah won the ACC Championship at Duke last year with Barkate as his top receiver (1,106 receiving yards). Even without Toney, Miami has more talented playmakers than CJ Carr and Notre Dame, and the Irish aren't healthy in their back seven. Notre Dame has ruled out linebacker Drayk Bowen, safety Tae Johnson, and cornerback DJ McKinney. Miami vs Notre Dame Over/Under pick: Over 54.5 With Mensah and Carr arguably the top two QBs in college football this season, I would play the Over at 55.5 or better , even with Toney out. Mensah is deadly accurate and ranks No. 1 in college football in TD passes (25), with Miami ranking No. 2 in the country in offensive success rate (52.4%). Notre Dame isn't far behind, though, sitting No. 4 in offensive success rate (51.4%) thanks to Carr, who r anks eighth in QBR (82.6), 11th in big-time throw rate (6.9%), and 18th in TD passes (18). Miami's pass defense has also been suspect at times, and Carr can take advantage. The Hurricanes are ranked just 110th in EPA per dropback. In the Fighting Irish's previous two games against teams ranked in the Top 50 by SP+ , they hit the Over. Miami vs Notre Dame prop: Miami TT Over 23.5 Toney is one of the best wide receivers in recent college football history, but Miami's offense has been a force with Mensah at QB and Dawson calling plays, and I don't think it will just collapse without its top receiver. I like the Hurricanes to hit the Over on their team total at 23.5 or better against a Notre Dame defense that allowed 28 points to BYU without its best offensive player, LJ Martin . Miami's passing attack is far more prolific than BYU's, with Miami's offense leading the country in EPA per dropback and net adjusted EPA per play. Notre Dame's defense has also been shaky on money downs this season, ranking 67th nationally in third/fourth down success rate (43.6%). Miami vs Notre Dame combo This is the "game of the century" of the week in college football and the No. 1 must-watch matchup in my Week 10 Top 25 predictions , featuring the season's most loaded slate. While Miami would certainly be an upset threat to Notre Dame with Toney, I don't think Mario Cristobal's team will roll over in its biggest game of the season. The Hurricanes ended last season by covering the spread in four straight College Football Playoff games , including three as an underdog. Cristobal knows how to get his team up, and Notre Dame has had slow starts in three of its last four games, failing to cover in all three of those games as a favorite . Photo By - Reuters Connect. Darian Mensah, CJ Carr, NCAAF. South Bend will be the epicenter of the college football universe on Saturday night when the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes roll into town to face the Notre Dame Fighting Irish. We won't get to see Malachi Toney in action, but our Miami vs. Notre Dame prop picks for this heavyweight bout focus on the showdown between elite quarterbacks Darian Mensah and CJ Carr. For more college football picks and analysis, check out Rob Paul's Miami vs. Notre Dame predictions ahead of kickoff at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 7. Best Miami vs Notre Dame props Prop pick #1: CJ Carr Over 4.5 rush attempts I gave out this same prop when Notre Dame faced BYU, and CJ Carr came through. I'm backing it again, up to 55%, for many of the same reasons. It starts with the game plan. This Miami defense ranks second in EPA per rush but 110th in EPA per pass. That means we'll likely see fewer handoffs and more dropback opportunities. That also puts Carr up against a Hurricanes front that ranks 15th in pass-rush grade, per PFF, and 29th nationally in sack rate. Carr has shown this season that he's not afraid to scramble. Factor in sacks counting as rush attempts, and he should clear this total for the fifth time in seven contests. Prop pick #2: Micah Gilbert Over 31.5 receiving yards Jordan Faison leads all Notre Dame receivers with 56 targets, while Jaden Greathouse and Micah Gilbert are tied with 33 targets apiece. But Gilbert is the player being undervalued here, and I'm backing him up to 54%. Miami's secondary isn't just struggling in coverage; it's also struggling to make tackles in the open field. Gilbert has the best yards after catch per reception (5.5) of Carr's top three targets and ranks second behind Faison in yards per route run. Gilbert is also the most reliable of the three, securing 72.7% of his targets. He's averaging 70.4 receiving yards in the six games in which he's run at least 20 routes. He's a bargain with a receiving yards line that's less than half of Faison's 69.5-yard total. Prop pick #3: Darian Mensah Over 1.5 passing touchdowns With Malachi Toney sidelined, Darian Mensah has an opportunity to take another step toward the Heisman tonight, and I'm backing him up to 55% to throw multiple touchdown passes. Not only do the Hurricanes rank third in red-zone scoring, but only Notre Dame has a higher offensive Eckel rate than Miami this season. As well as Notre Dame defends, the Irish are depleted on the back end heading into this game. Defensive captain Drayk Bowen is out at linebacker, and the secondary will be without DJ McKinney and Tae Johnson. The Irish gave up three touchdown passes to UNC's Billy Edwards, one of the few quality passers they've faced this season. Mensah leads the nation in passing efficiency and completion rate, and getting him at this number is a gift. Sep 19, 2026; South Bend, Indiana, USA; Notre Dame Fighting Irish quarterback CJ Carr (13) looks on after the game against the Michigan State Spartans at Notre Dame Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Nick Shepkowski · Notre Dame Fighting Irish On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:28 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the first time in exactly seven years, Notre Dame welcomes the No. 1 team in the nation to South Bend. Like last time, when top-ranked an unbeaten Clemson came to town late in the 2020 season, another ACC foe brings an unbeaten an No. 1 ranking. This time its the mighty Miami Hurricanes and the rivalry between the two programs is as strong as ever. So does Notre Dame knock off No. 1? Or does Miami leave South Bend with the No. 1 overall seed in the College Football Playoff seemingly on ice? Here's what the matchups favor on Saturday night in South Bend: When Miami Has the Ball Malachi Toney or not , this Miami offense is like few in all of college football. Sure, its biggest playmaker is out, but can Notre Dame slow down the thunder and lightning running attack of Javian Mallory and Mark Fletcher? Furthermore, Darian Mensah has 25 touchdown passes to just one interception all season long. Can Notre Dame's defense, which will be playing a bit shorthanded itself, keep Miami in check enough? That has been a major issue in the biggest games over the last two seasons. Advantage: Miami When Notre Dame Has the Ball Notre Dame has one of the better offensive lines in college football but has its work cut out against this Miami defensive front. The Hurricanes are allowing just 2.4 yards per rush attempt this year, which means Notre Dame likely won't be able to play the same ball possession type game it likes to. That means CJ Carr's moment is now: Miami has a pass defense that has surrendered huge numbers in narrow escapes against both Florida State and North Carolina. Can Carr do enough to win what could very possibly turn into a track meet between the powerhouse programs? Advantage: Notre Dame Special Teams For the Win? So far we're pretty much at a toss-up, and we figure special teams will end up being huge. Notre Dame doesn't have to have a kick return for a touchdown to win this thing, but overall, its numbers in kick return, punt return, kick coverage, and punt coverage give the Irish an advantage statisically. Factor in a veteran kicker in Spencer Porath who is Notre Dame's best at the position in years and special teams coordinator Marty Biagi, who has had a bit of a quiet year by his standards, to date, and I expect to see the Irish steal a possession and deciding score as a result. Nick Shepkowski's Prediction: Saturday night ends with CJ Carr suddenly being the Heisman Trophy front runner after he throws for 350 yards, four touchdowns, and leads a late drive that ends with a Notre Dame field goal as time expires. The No. 1 ranked Miami Hurricanes are in town to play the No. 4 ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish, and the stakes are about as high as they get for ND. If the Irish lose, the season is basically over — even with three regular season games left on the schedule. If Notre Dame wins… the path to the playoff and a first round bye is illuminated. With no USC on the schedule this year, having an old rival like Miami being in this position only makes things even grander than all of the hype and hoopla a top 4 matchup brings with College Gameday in attendance. This is a GIANT of a game, and you have to be ready for it. While I absolutely prefer the Gulf of Mexico side of Florida, I do appreciate the flavors and culture of Miami — but I also love mashups. Toney isn't just the best WR on Miami's team, he's one of the best players in the country — period. He's so good, that when he's not in the game, Miami's "potent offense" goes to shit — and Darian Mensah looks like a Duke QB and not the QB of the No.1 ranked Canes. Notre Dame is backed into a corner, and I believe that will create the sense of urgency needed to come out and dominate the game early, and then ride out a win late. Notre Dame 34, Miami 20

Reyna, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Wed, November 4, 2026 at 10:46 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Notre Dame football gets the marquee stage in the collegiate world Saturday. This time with No. 1 ranked Miami (FL) football back in South Bend for the first time since 2016. Yet Hurricanes coach Mario Cristobal likely remembers the revered 1988 matchup with the Fighting Irish. He was a true freshman offensive lineman for the famed "Catholics versus Convicts" showdown. ND fans took pregame marketing tactics to another level with the famed shirt and game nickname. That fourth-ranked Fighting Irish team knocked off the top-ranked 'Canes 31-30. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Fast forward 38 years later, and Miami enters this venue undefeated and No. 1 again. But will the nation see similar results from that '88 meeting? Or can the Hurricanes prevail this time around? It's time to dive into the bold predictions for this highly-anticipated showdown. CJ Carr and Darian Mensah puts on a show, but one seals Heisman fate Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Mensah is arguably the nation's hottest quarterback. He brings an astonishing 25:1 touchdown-to-interception ratio into Notre Dame Stadium. Carr, meanwhile, owns 18 touchdown throws. But he matches Mensah's interception number too. Both will launch the field version of fireworks. Except Carr is facing a Miami defense's that's looked suspect in recent weeks. The 'Canes have surrendered between 23 to 35 points in the last three games. Even North Carolina quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. picked apart Miami with 341 passing yards and four touchdowns. Miami is built for shootouts thanks to Mensah handing this offense a throwing and running element. ND recently struggled with one dual-threat already in BYU's Bear Bachmeier, who combined for 269 yards and three touchdowns in the Cougars' 28-24 upset on Oct. 18. Both will put on a show. But the winning quarterback will seal his Heisman Trophy fate here. Malachi Toney won't try to sit So there's a new curveball that surfaced for this heavyweight showdown of storied programs. Miami wide receiver Malachi Toney sustained an ankle injury during Wednesday practice . Now Miami fans are on pins and needles wondering if he'll sit this one out. But there's the feeling he'll try to avoid sitting. This game comes with hefty implications impacting who could get the top seed in the College Football Playoff. Plus this Hurricanes team has been on a mission since their National Championship Game loss to Indiana. Toney only sits if his ankle injury is way severe than originally thought. If anything, Cristobal and offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson may consider handing Toney a pitch count type of approach by limiting his usage. Leonard Moore's NFL Draft fate gets sealed Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Moore versus Toney certainly is one individual battle fans want to see. The Fighting Irish cornerback still plays an integral role for this defense even if Toney doesn't play. And he'll seal his NFL Draft fate with this game. Moore frustrating Mensah and forcing him into errant decisions can boost his stock. Same with taking away Miami's second-best option Cooper Barkate. But NFL scouts and perhaps general managers will be locked into how Moore performs against one or two Heisman Trophy contenders. This is the game that can turn him into the nation's most pro ready CB, and a potential top five pick (CBS Sports plugs him at No. 3 overall to the Miami Dolphins). This will be a close contest and shootout, but the winner is? © Jasen Vinlove-Imagn Images Miami has withstood high-scoring affairs and is proving to win close games. Notre Dame's defense hasn't allowed 30 points in a game yet this season. This feels like a close shootout. But Toney's injury and Miami's sudden lack of bottling air attacks swings the edge to Notre Dame. Hence why the Fighting Irish will feed off the sellout crowd energy and turn Miami into the third No. 1 team to lose during the 2026 regular season. away.headline: Malachi Toney injury update: Early expectation has Miami star WR returning in time for postseason run
away.blurb: No. 1 Miami may be without star receiver Malachi Toney against No. 11 Notre Dame on Saturday, but the team hopes to have him back in time for the postseason. Sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz that the early feel on a return timetable is that Toney is expected to miss four to six weeks after undergoing ankle surgery. Toney suffered a high-ankle sprain in practice this week that will knock him out for the rest of the regular season, but the team hopes surgery will help the sophomore receiver return in time to chase a national championship. Based on that timeline, the Hurricanes could get Toney back in time for the ACC Championship Game. Depending on how the rest of the Canes' regular season plays out, they may not even need to risk playing him in that game. If the Hurricanes can pull out a win over the Fighting Irish on Saturday night, it's hard to see them slipping up in the regular season. Their final three games are against Duke , Virginia Tech and Boston College , all of which are at home. At this point, the conference title game may be more risk than reward for Toney and Miami. Prior to his injury, Toney was building a strong case for the Heisman Trophy as he leads the ACC in receptions (73), receiving yards (1,027) and receiving touchdowns (13). With Toney out of the lineup, Miami will need someone else to step up and replace his production with Duke transfer Cooper Barkate being the most obvious candidate. Even if Toney's recovery winds up taking closer to six weeks, that's plenty of time for him to be healthy for the College Football Playoff. The first round doesn't kick off until Dec. 18, and if Miami earns a top-four seed and first-round bye, it wouldn't play until Dec. 30 at the earliest. It also helps that Miami has another Heisman candidate leading its offense at quarterback, Darian Mensah. Facing Notre Dame's defense on the road may be the toughest test Mensah has gotten all season, but he's made it look easy to this point, throwing for 25 touchdowns and just one interception. Although the loss of Toney puts a damper on tonight's matchup, it remains one of the biggest games of the season. The Hurricanes need as much wiggle room as they can get with Toney set to miss the month of November, and the Fighting Irish clearly need a signature win after the initial College Football Playoff Rankings placed them at No. 11.

away.headline: Notre Dame’s Marcus Freeman raises questions about Miami’s Malachi Toney status
away.blurb: The Notre Dame Fighting Irish may have caught a break before their showdown with No. 1 Miami, but Marcus Freeman isn’t treating the reported loss of Malachi Toney as a reason to throw out the defensive game plan. In a Thursday report, On3’s Daniel Hager highlighted Freeman’s refusal to assume the Miami receiver would be unavailable. Toney rolled his ankle during Wednesday’s practice, and On3’s Pete Nakos and Brett McMurphy reported he would undergo TightRope surgery and be sidelined indefinitely. A return later in the season remains possible. In Toney’s college debut, he caught six passes for 82 yards and a touchdown as Miami beat Notre Dame 27-24. That result later proved critical when Miami earned a College Football Playoff berth and the Irish were left out. The Irish will be missing defensive help of their own. Linebacker Drayk Bowen is out with an ankle injury, and safety Brauntae Johnson and cornerback DJ McKinney also remain unavailable. Toney, the Hurricanes’ leading receiver and one of college football’s top playmakers, reportedly needs surgery after injuring his ankle Wednesday. He is expected to miss Saturday’s game in South Bend. Freeman, however, says Notre Dame still intends to prepare for him. Notre Dame’s Marcus Freeman Addresses Malachi Toney Injury Uncertainty “We’ll see if he plays or not,” Freeman said. “We have to make sure we have a plan if he plays, if he doesn’t, we’ll adjust.” Miami isn’t required to release an ACC availability report for Saturday’s game. The conference mandates those reports for conference matchups, and Notre Dame is a nonconference opponent. That leaves the Irish without the usual conference-mandated injury updates on Toney unless Miami voluntarily provides them. Miami confirmed the practice injury Wednesday but did not publicly provide a surgical timetable. ESPN subsequently reported that Toney is expected to miss Notre Dame and likely several more weeks. Freeman revealed that he learned of the injury after practice Wednesday, leaving Notre Dame only the final days of preparation to consider an offense without its top receiver. Earlier, Freeman called Toney “one of one,” according to The Associated Press’ Tim Reynolds . Miami’s Malachi Toney Absence Would Test Hurricanes Offense The sophomore has 73 receptions for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns through eight games in 2026. Those totals rank second nationally in catches, third in receiving yards and tied for second in touchdown receptions. He accounted for more than a third of Miami’s receptions and receiving yards before the injury. Against North Carolina last Saturday, Toney had seven catches for 75 yards and two touchdowns in a 38-35 victory. But Freeman isn’t planning on Miami’s offense disappearing without him. As ESPN’s Adam Rittenberg reported, Freeman emphasized Miami’s roster depth. “It’s not always the position as much as it is the player,” he said. Cooper Barkate is Miami’s next-leading receiver with 28 catches for 372 yards and four touchdowns

Reports said Toney suffered a high ankle sprain on Wednesday, Nov. 4, and that he would undergo surgery, putting not only the showdown with the No. 6 Fighting Irish out of the question, but the rest of his stellar season in jeopardy. Toney has battled injuries throughout the season, briefly leaving games against Wake Forest on Sept. 18, Clemson on Oct. 3, Florida State on Oct. 17 and Pittsburgh on Oct. 24. He never went back to the locker room, though his limited play late against Wake can be explicitly tied to the offense's stagnation and one of their closest games of the season. And he was able to shake off his injury vs. Pitt en route to breaking his own Miami record with 16 catches for 194 yards and three touchdowns. When will Malachi Toney return? According to the Cleveland Clinic , high ankle sprains occur when the ligaments that attach the tibia to the fibula near the foot are torn or damaged. Recovery takes six to eight weeks, though the Clinic says it might take longer for athletes to return to play. However, there is hope Toney can return sooner, with initial reports indicating he could return in time for the College Football Playoff. The first round of the CFP is Dec. 18-19, six weeks away. If Miami retains one of the top four spots in the final CFP rankings (they're No. 1 heading into today's game at Notre Dame), they would first play in the quarterfinals Dec. 30 or Jan. 1, in about eight weeks. There's a chance Toney could return for the ACC championship game Dec. 5, four weeks from now. Former Notre Dame and current Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love suffered a high ankle sprain last week. Initial reports indicate he could return as soon as he comes off injured reserve for the minimum four weeks. Who benefits if Malachi Toney is out vs Notre Dame? There's no bigger reason for why the Miami football team has been a contender to win the national championship than explosive wide receiver Malachi Toney . Throughout the season, the 19-year-old sophomore has been the best player on the No. 1 team in the country, one that also features a quarterback in Darian Mensah who's completed 80% of his passes, ranks in the top 10 nationally in passing yards and touchdowns, and has coupled that with just one interception. Toney is the reason all that has been possible, and there aren't a lot of college football fans who would argue that. The Bulldogs came back from a nine-point fourth-quarter deficit in the first meeting, outscoring the Rebels 17-0 in the fourth to win 43-35, but Ole Miss would have its revenge. It was in the College Football Playoff quarterfinal at the Sugar Bowl that the Rebels ended Georgia's season with a 39-34 win thanks largely to the heroics of quarterback Trinidad Chambliss . So what will these two deliver this year? While plenty has changed from last year's teams to this year, both quarterbacks return, and there are high stakes involved here. Georgia debuted at No. 2 in the first College Football Playoff rankings of the season, and a win here would solidify their chances of reaching the SEC Championship. On the other side, the Rebels need a win to gain firmer ground. They're No. 10 in the rankings, putting them on the precipice of losing an at-large bid. Plus, a loss here would be their third in SEC play, essentially ending their conference title hopes, and putting them in a position where they need to win out and hope for some other teams to lose to return to the playoff . Georgia vs. Ole Miss: Need to know This is the fifth straight time these two have met while ranked: Maybe that doesn't seem like something that's all that impressive to you, but for context, it had happened only five times in the first 46 meetings between the schools. Georgia has had the better end of most meetings, as they lead the series 34-14-1, and a win for Ole Miss this weekend would give the Rebels consecutive wins over the Dawgs for the first time since the 1995 and 1996 seasons. Kirby Smart has done well against ranked opponents: The Georgia coach is 44-18 against AP-ranked teams during his tenure in Athens. That's the fifth-best record by any head coach against ranked teams in AP Poll history (minimum of 20 games). That includes a stretch of six wins in their last seven against ranked teams. The last loss? To Ole Miss in the playoff last year. Trinidad Chambliss could tie a school record here: Chambliss has thrown for at least one touchdown in 21 consecutive games. If he throws one against Georgia, it will put him in a tie with former Ole Miss QB Chad Kelly for most consecutive games with a TD pass at 22. picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs. Georgia Predictions: Who Wins? Our Staff Picks and Final Scores Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS No. 10 Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2) and No. 2 Georgia (7-1, 5-1) are set to square off on Saturday , in what will mark one of the biggest and most consequential games in the history of Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. In order to maintain control of its College Football Playoff destiny, Ole Miss will have to knock off Georgia for the third time in the program’s last four matchups. With a loss, the Rebels will put their season resume in the hands of the playoff committee with little optimism of returning to meaningful postseason play. Considering what Ole Miss has left in the final quarter of its season, there would be a lot of ground to make up. Ahead of the Rebels' top-10 matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Ole Miss Rebels On SI Staff Predictions Oct 18, 2025; Athens, Georgia, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) runs the ball for a touchdown against Mississippi Rebels defensive tackle Will Echoles (52) during the first half of the game at Sanford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matt Galatzan Matt Galatzan The last two times these two teams met, both games were absolute cinema. Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels offense was unstoppable in both matchups, particularly in Round 2, when they knocked of the Bulldogs in the College Football Playoff. This year, the calculus has changed a bit. The Rebels have a new play caller, and new weapons on the outside. The Defense has also been struggling as of late. On the other side, the Bulldogs are built on defense, running the football and controlling the clock - exactly where Ole Miss has been exploited defensively. For Ole Miss to win here, I think Chambliss - especially without Kewan Lacy in the lineup - is going to have to be Superman. We have seen him do it before plenty of times, but if the Bulldogs can deploy a similar game plan that Texas did two weeks ago, it could be a long day. Shekai Mills-Knight could be an X-factor, but it's hard to be able to rely on a redshirt freshman on a stage like this. The Rebels do have an elite home field advantage, but at the end of the day, I think it all comes down to the Rebels defense and if they can hold up against the Georgia run game. I'll take the Dawgs in a tight one. Georgia 31, Ole Miss 27 Understandably, almost everyone had the LSU game circled on Ole Miss’ schedule going into the season. If Georgia packs its usual run game and efficiency stopping the run, it could be a long night for the Rebels. Although there is reason to have optimism about the Rebels’ side of those two aspects. September and October couldn’t have looked any different for Ole Miss, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Offensively, Trinidad Chambliss will need to play a game similar to the one he played against LSU all the way back in Week 3. The version of Chambliss we saw against Auburn was the next closest thing, and he’ll have to continue adding yards with his legs even on plays that aren’t broken down. Without Kewan Lacy, Ole Miss will need efficiency from Chambliss, Makhi Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight on the ground. The Rebels will also desperately need a bounce back game from one of its most explosive players in Deuce Alexander Ole Miss was in an eerily similar spot in November of the 2024 season. Like that weekend, I’m picking the Rebels to get the job done again against Georgia, but it should be much closer than the game that was last played in Oxford between these two. Ole Miss 34, Georgia 31 With the Rebels already having two losses this season, I think Saturday night’s game is a must-win to keep their playoff hopes strong. That should translate into a motivated team and an electric environment in Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, and when playing in The Vaught, especially at night, there isn’t a team in the country I’d take over Ole Miss. The Rebels are 26-1 at home since 2023, including a victory over the Bulldogs in the 2024 regular season that had very similar stakes as this game. Picking any team, let alone one that’s been as hot and cold as Ole Miss has been at times this season, to beat the No. 2 team in the country could age poorly. Despite that, give me Pete Golding, Trinidad Chambliss and the rest of the Ole Miss Rebels to win and keep their playoff and SEC Championship ambitions alive and send the Rebel fans home happy on Saturday night. Ole Miss 31, Georgia 24 Zion Trammell Pete Golding’s biggest challenge is slowing down Georgia’s rushing attack. The Bulldogs average 200 rushing yards per game, and if Ole Miss can’t stop it, the Rebels could struggle to pull ahead. Golding will need Trinidad Chambliss to deliver if Ole Miss is going to defeat Georgia. If the Rebels consistently get off the field on third down and establish their offensive rhythm, I think Ole Miss gets a huge win. Ole Miss 28, Georgia 24 Cooper Ferguson A budding rivalry between two of the SEC’s top programs. We’re in for a barnburner at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium tomorrow night. Trinidad Chambliss is beginning to look like himself again, and with the Rebels offensive line performing about as good as ever before, I expect an incredible offensive showing from the home side. Kirby Smart’s side will never go down easy, and Gunnar Stockton is a solid leader for the Bulldogs offense. Sparks will fly in Oxford, but a repeat of 2024 is in order. picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football vs. Ole Miss Football on Saturday Night Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Georgia Bulldogs and the Ole Miss Rebels will face off on Saturday night in Oxford, Mississippi in one of college football's most anticipated matchups. These two teams played twice last year. One game was in Athens and one was in the Sugar Bowl for a College Football Playoff quarterfinal game. Both were epic showdowns that involved second half comebacks. So that means that Kirby Smart and Pete Golding could be in for another back and forth game. These two teams feature some of the best players in the entire county. Georgia is favored, and advanced stats point this in Georgia’s favor, but Ole Miss has Trinidad Chambliss and the home crowd. Let’s make three bold predictions: Georgia Sacks Trinidad Chambliss at Least Three Times This is a different Georgia defense that Chambliss will be facing off against. Last year, the Dawgs managed just 20 sacks in 14 games. They are up to 26 this season in only eight games. Georgia didn’t take Chambliss down behind the line of scrimmage a single time in either matchup a season ago. Part of that was because of the magician-like escapability Chambliss showed off in new Orleans. This year is different for this defense and Chris Cole has leveled up to be one of the biggest difference makers on that side of the ball in all of college football. Georgia has gotten to the quarterback in big games this year, and Chambliss’ pocket presence and athleticism makes three sacks a bold prediction. Pick your champion (you can change it later). Dawgs Clear 200 Yards on the Ground, Again Georgia is averaging 200 yards per game on the ground. They hit that number on the road against Alabama. They hit that number last week against the Florida Gators. Ole Miss has shown that you can run all over them if you get a lead. Florida bullied the Rebels down in Gainesville, totalling 302 yards on the ground. That was when Florida was a lot more explosive on offense, but still, Ole Miss showed it was possible. Georgia is clearly a run-first offense, and Nate Frazier looked a lot closer to the Nate Frazier we saw at the beginning of the season in Georgia’s win last week. His health would bring a huge boost to the run game, making the explosive Dwight Phillips Jr. a complimentary weapon and a change of pace back. Chambliss Gets Picked Twice The only SEC games where Georgia wasn’t forcing turnovers were against Auburn and Vanderbilt. Even then, they did get an interception against the Commodores. Georgia’s defense has been a lot more opportunistic this season. A handful of different players have forced fumbles. Eliis Robinson IV is shaping up to be a first-round pick. Demello Jones is forcing turnovers. Even Braylon Conley got an interception last week. Chambliss has thrown eight interceptions already this season. He only threw three all last year. He is being asked to do more because Ole Miss is not running the football as well, and Ole Miss is getting into deficits. Georgia’s defense is the best they will face all year. Even if Ole Miss wins or it is close, two interceptions is completely possible against a vaunted Dawgs defense. My Georgia vs. Ole Miss prediction and college football picks for tonight expect Kirby Smart's defense to rise to the occasion against Trinidad Chambliss & Co. as the Bulldogs seek revenge for last year's Sugar Bowl loss to the Rebels. Georgia is a 3.5-point favorite as it visits Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Miss., on Saturday, Nov. 7, while the total sits at 56.5. Don't miss kickoff at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. TOP PICK Who will win Georgia vs Ole Miss today: Georgia -3.5 Georgia and Ole Miss played two wild shootouts last year, with the Bulldogs winning the regular-season matchup and the Rebels taking it in the Sugar Bowl. This time around, I like Georgia to cover as many as 6.5 points on the road against Ole Miss. Defense will be the difference in the matchup this year, with Georgia having one of the best in the country ( ranked No. 2 by SP+ ), and Ole Miss' being one of the worst in the SEC. With the Rebels down All-American running back Kewan Lacy , the Bulldogs' defense can lock in on stopping Trinidad Chambliss . Chambliss has faced one other defense ranked top five by SP+, Texas , and struggled in a loss. Against the Longhorns, he threw three interceptions and put up a season-low 60% adjusted completion percentage. Georgia vs Ole Miss Over/Under pick: Under 56.5 Though both games between these teams last year were full of points, Georgia's defense should keep it relatively low-scoring this time around, and I would play the Under at 55.5 or better . The Bulldogs' defense ranks top 20 nationally in available yards percentage (33.5%) , havoc rate (19.4%), and success rate allowed (35.2%). With no Lacy for Ole Miss, it'll put even more on Chambliss, who has frequently had to carry the team this season, and we saw that approach fall flat against Texas. However, Georgia's offense hasn't been lighting up the scoreboard lately either, averaging just 23.6 points per game in its last three outings. So while this is one of the must-watch matchups in my Week 10 Top 25 predictions , it's not because I'm expecting another shootout. Georgia vs Ole Miss combo Ole Miss is a feast-or-famine type of team. The Rebels beat LSU and Missouri , but were blown out by Florida and fell behind so quickly against Texas that they couldn't dig themselves out. That's what happens when you lean so heavily on a star QB to make up for an inconsistent run game and one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Against Georgia, Chambliss won't be Superman; Smart has too much NFL talent on a defense that's allowed more than 20 points just once this season. If Ole Miss falls behind, Georgia's offense will lean on Gunner Stockton to manage the game and take a ball-control approach against a Rebels defense ranked 88th in the country in EPA per rush. Ole Miss team total Under 26.5 Georgia team total Over 30.5 Georgia vs Ole Miss prop: Ole Miss team total Under 26.5 Chambliss can only do so much, and against a freakishly athletic and long Georgia defense, I don't think Ole Miss will be scoring at nearly as high a clip as it has against lesser SEC teams. I would take the Under on Ole Miss' team total at 24.5 or better . Georgia linebacker Chris Cole is arguably the best defensive player in the country, and Glenn Schumann and Kirby Smart could deploy him as a Chambliss stopper. With 4.5 40-yard dash speed and nearly 34-inch arms, Cole has earned his nickname of "Tarantula." Look for the Bulldogs to spy Chambliss with him and use him as a blitzer too; he leads Georgia in pressures (24) and pass-rush win rate (17.4%). With Cole hunting Chambliss and the Bulldogs' defense ranking top 20 in rush success rate (37.8%), Ole Miss will struggle to find the end zone. The Bottom Line Georgia needs to establish its rushing attack, pressure Chambliss, and take advantage of its defensive superiority. Ole Miss needs explosive quarterback play, improved rushing production, and an early lead to build on. The biggest question: Can Ole Miss' offense generate enough against one of the nation's top-scoring defenses, particularly without its leading running back? away.headline: Georgia football WR Isiah Canion nowhere to be found on UGA's injury report
away.source: Dawn of the Dawg on MSN
away.blurb: Isiah Canion was one of Georgia's biggest acquisitions out of the Transfer Portal this offseason. He came to Georgia after spending two seasons at Georgia Tech, and he was expected to be a central piece of the Bulldogs' passing attack this year. He unfortunately was hurt during the second game of Georgia's season and hasn't seen the field since. Earlier this week though he was marked probable to play on Georgia's official injury report and on Thursday he was nowhere to be found on their report which means he has been officially cleared to play. This injury update does need to be taken with a grain of salt. Nate Frazier came off Georgia's injury report heading into the Alabama game, but he still didn't play. Based on that it still isn't a 100 percent guarantee that Canion will play against Ole Miss, but he most likely will be available. Chauncey Bowens still questionable to play vs Ole Miss While it looks like Georgia will finally be getting Canion back, the same can't be said for running back Chauncey Bowens. On Thursday's injury report he was still listed as questionable to play, so there is a chance he will be able to suit up against the Rebels. There however is just as good of a chance that he won't be able to play either. Another injury report will come out Friday night before one final injury update about an hour before kickoff on Saturday. Georgia's injured 3-headed monster could all return in time to play Florida Georgia WR Isiah Canion injury update is great news for UGA Canion has only recorded three receptions for 28 yards this season. That can't be held against him though because the starters barely played in Georgia's season opener against Tennessee State before he got hurt the following week in Week 2. Canion has a lot of potential though that Georgia hasn't seen yet. Last year at Georgia Tech he was an integral part of their talented offense as he recorded 33 receptions for 480 yards and four touchdowns.
