home.blurb: Friday Ole Miss vs. Georgia Injury Report: Keaton Thomas Probable - The Rebel Walk Recent ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – Ole Miss linebacker Keaton Thomas is probable for Saturday night's game against No. 2 Georgia after being questionable on Thursday, according to the SEC's Friday availability report. Defensive end Kam Franklin remains questionable. The report was posted at 7:10 p.m. CT on Friday. Ole Miss' list of players who are out did not change, with running back Kewan Lacy and eight others ruled out again. Georgia, meanwhile, moved three players from questionable to out: inside linebacker AJ Kruah , safety Tyriq Green and defensive lineman Joseph Jonah-Ajonye . Keaton Thomas moves up to probable Thomas, a linebacker, was questionable on both Wednesday and Thursday and is now probable for Saturday night. That is the only change to the Ole Miss availability designations from Thursday. Cornerback Jalyn Crawford and safety MJ Preston remain probable, and no other Rebels are listed. Kam Franklin remains questionable Franklin has carried the questionable tag all week and has not been cleared with kickoff about 23 hours away. He has 25 tackles, including 15 solo stops and 10 assists, along with 5.0 tackles for loss, two sacks, a pass breakup and a fumble recovery he returned for a touchdown through eight games this season. He was named a leader of the defense in our September feature on Franklin . Without him, Ole Miss would lose one of its best pass rushers and run stoppers against a Georgia offense that scores 41 points per game. Georgia's report got shorter on the questionable side and longer on the out side. Kruah, Green and Jonah-Ajonye were all questionable on Thursday and are now out, joining outside linebacker Amaris Williams, who has been out all week. Tight end Elyiss Williams remains questionable. Wide receiver Thomas Blackshear and running back Chauncey Bowens were questionable Thursday and are now probable. " My Week 10 college football picks lean toward a low-scoring defensive slugfest down in Gainesville. TOP PICK Who will win Oklahoma vs. Florida today: Florida -6.5 I'm laying the points with Florida at -7 or better. Oklahoma 's season is a bust. Jason Witten will call plays for the first time at the college level, and Brent Venables said that "everything is on the table" at quarterback given John Mateer 's struggles ( 13 touchdown passes, seven interceptions, and two lost fumbles ). The once-vaunted defense has also shown signs of mortality, ranking ninth nationally in EPA per play allowed but 112th in explosiveness allowed . This is a buy-low spot on Florida , which has lost three of its last four games. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Sat, November 7, 2026 at 2:18 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When we last saw Oklahoma and Florida play, the Sooners rolled 55-20 in the 2020 Cotton Bowl over a high-powered Gator team that lost to eventual national champion Alabama in an epic SEC Championship. The other meeting was the BCS Championship at the end of the 2009 season, when Tim Tebow and the Gator defense took down Heisman-winner Sam Bradford and the amazing Sooner attack 24-14 for the national title. The stakes aren't as high this time around, but for a Florida program that's on the rise, and No. 24 in the first College Football Playoff rankings, and for a 4-4 Oklahoma desperate to close strong, this will be intense. Oklahoma vs Florida: Quick Hits Oklahoma at 4-4, needs to win two of its last four to be bowl eligible. It hosts Ole Miss and Texas A&M after this before closing at Missouri. Florida is coming off the 27-8 loss to Georgia. It goes to Kentucky next, hosts Vanderbilt, and finishes at Florida State. Again, the first two meetings were in big bowl games. This is the first regular season matchup between the two. How To Watch Oklahoma vs Florida Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 7:45 PM ET TV: SEC Network Location: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville, FL – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Oklahoma Will Win The defense continues to fight the good fight. It had a problem in the 42-25 loss to South Carolina, but the defense is fantastic on third downs thanks to a pass rush that takes over games. But to beat Florida, you have to slow down the run. The Gators are 0-3 when running for fewer than 155 yards, and the Sooners give up just 107 yards per game. Only Mississippi State and, last week, South Carolina have been able to gash the Sooners for more. Why Florida Will Win Oklahoma's offense has a hard time running the ball. With a defense as good as the Sooners have, all the O has to do is keep it moving and not screw it up. But no running game means more pressing overall, and then come the mistakes. The Sooners only average 107 yards per game on the ground, and they just can't find any room to move. The Gators have to hold up, and then pounce on an Oklahoma attack that turned it over four times against both Georgia and Kentucky, three times against New Mexico, and twice against Michigan. Oklahoma vs Florida Prediction, Betting Lines It's stupid, but if you buy into these things, going back to the last two games of last season, Oklahoma is on a ten-game run of alternating wins and losses. The Sooners beat Texas, then lost to Kentucky, beat Mississippi State, lost to South Carolina, beat … Florida? The Sooners have the defense to hold up and make Florida struggle. The Gators got by Texas a few weeks ago, but it's been a struggle, losing three of the last four. Weird trends aside, this Oklahoma team really does have a way of rallying when it absolutely has to. The Sooners need to win two of their final four to earn bowl eligibility . With a new voice leading the offense, the Sooners are hoping for a turnaround to end the 2026 season. Jason Witten takes over an offense that has underachieved this season, given the number of returning starters along the offensive line and the weapons at returning quarterback John Mateer. How much better can Oklahoma be in a week is the question on everyone's minds. It's unlikely the Sooners will suddenly erupt on offense, but if they find more consistency, they'll have a chance to finish the season on a high note. So how will the Sooners perform in "The Swamp?" Our staff here at Sooners Wire picked this week's showdown between the Sooners and the Gators. Too Many Questions Oklahoma tight ends coach Jason Witten, left, talks with coach Brent Venables during a Sooners football spring practice in Norman, Okla., Thursday, April 9, 2026. There are just too many moving parts for Oklahoma to reliably believe the Sooners could win a road game in the swamp. The Sooners have made a change at offensive coordinator and the availability of a bunch of notable players on both sides of the ball are still in question. There's also the question of how Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer will play without Ben Arbuckle on the sideline for the first time in years. Even though Florida has a few issues to worry about as well, they're certainly not as dire as Oklahoma's at the moment. Florida 21, Oklahoma 10 James D. Jackson, Contributor Improved Sooners Touchdowns? Touchdowns. Oklahoma made a huge move this week by letting go of Ben Arbuckle and having Jason Witten call plays. Witten called plays as a high school head coach and had a ton of success doing it. I think the offense will play with a fire we haven't seen this year, and the defense will return to its dominant ways. Because of that, I've got OU winning and the offense scoring three touchdowns. For now, though, the only change is the absence of OC Ben Arbuckle, so all of Oklahoma's other offensive problems remain. Expect OU's defense to bounce back against Florida, but expect the offense to continue faltering for the remainder of this season. Expect the defense to bounce back and play well against Jaden Baugh and the Gators' rushing attack, but with injury concerns in the secondary, the Sooners may have a hard time slowing down Tramell Jones. Florida was blown out a week ago by the Georgia Bulldogs, seeing them drop their third game of the season. But the Gators have been a resilient group all year long, and this team will be asked to make it happen again. Entering the game, the Gators hold a record of 5-3 on the year, with the team going 3-3 so far in SEC games. Florida is ranked at No. 23 for the week, staying alive in the first edition of the College Football Playoff rankings. As for the Sooners, they will be coming into the game with a record of 4-4 for the year, going 2-3 in SEC play so far. This team has underperformed this season, but the Gators can't overlook them at all. Oklahoma still has star quarterback John Mateer under center, and he can do damage against this Gators defense. Florida is going to have to be very careful in the game, looking to avoid being upset at home. As the two teams prepare for the SEC battle, the Gators are being favored to come away with the win this week. Florida has been given a 64 percent chance to take down Oklahoma at home, according to the ESPN matchup predictor . One way for the Gators to get an edge in the game is to get running back Jadan Baugh back into a strong rhythm. After an incredible start to the season, the star back has slowed down heavily, with him going 100 yards on the ground for four straight games. Baugh still has put together a special season for Florida, with him rushing for 801 yards with 13 touchdowns. But when the Gators are at their best, Baugh is going up and down the field, opening the offense up. If Florida is able to get Baugh going again this week, it could help the offense out, giving the team a much stronger chance to take down the Sooners. Oklahoma can have an explosive offensive attack, so the Gators may be forced to put up points in order to keep up with them. Kickoff for this game between the Gators and the Sooners is scheduled for 4:45 p.m. PT/7:45 p.m. ET from Ben Hill Griffin Stadium in Gainesville.

picks.headline: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida?
picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL trade deadline grades Latest CFP rankings Tatum, Celtics rout Brown, Sixers NFL trade deadline tracker Vikings trade for Cousins Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? Oklahoma Sooners tight ends coach Jason Witten will take over as interim offensive coordinator for the rest of the season. | Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Gators have an impressive resume, having beaten No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28 at The Swamp, then going on the road to Austin and taking down No. 7 Texas 27-24 - one week after OU beat them in Dallas - on a night the underwhelming Florida defense overwhelmed Arch Manning and the Longhorns, sacking him five times, limiting UT to 2-of-10 on third down (they had 13 first downs total) and holding the Horns to 272 total yards. But they were also blown out in back-to-back losses to No. 25 Missouri and unranked South Carolina, which preceded last week's 27-8 loss to No. 3 Georgia. Oklahoma is a touchdown underdog to Florida, but the Sooners are the best defense the Gators face. Still, OU may be reeling after its worst defensive performance in years in the blowout loss to South Carolina - which included an incomprehensible 25 missed tackles (usually 10 is a bad number). OU's first trip to The Swamp will be punctuated by another big game from Gators RB Jaden Baugh, who's third in the SEC at 100.3 rushing yards per game and first with 13 rushing TDs. Final score: Florida 28, Oklahoma 21 Things could get gross Saturday night. Florida has officially made a quarterback change, and Tramell Jones Jr. could be without a pair of key weapons to pair with an already banged up offensive line. Oklahoma's offense has been so bad it got its coordinator fired, but Jason Witten has never called plays collegiately and John Mateer is still likely the quarterback the Sooners will roll with. OU's defense needs to bounce back after its tackling struggles last week, but even an improved showing could see Gator running back Jaden Baugh have enough success to push Jon Sumrall's team across the finish line. Final: Florida 16, Oklahoma 13 OU is set up for further disaster as it heads to the swamp. Jason Witten will serve as the Sooners' play caller for the first time at the college level, John Mateer is still the quarterback and Ben Hill Griffin Stadium is one of the nation's most hostile atmospheres. But amid the weirdness, I expect OU to win this game. Teams often come out more inspired after a notable firing, and I predict Witten will lead a creative game plan as he auditions for the full-time offensive coordinator role. Florida's offense is good - but it is also prone to turning the ball over. If the Sooners are able to put pressure on Tramell Jones Jr. early, it will create a long day for the Gators' offense. Final: Oklahoma 24, Florida 20 The Sooners figure to get a little boost from Jason Witten's playcalling, but don't expect massive changes in either scheme or production here. The offensive line still has its issues, John Mateer hasn't been consistent at all, and neither of the other quarterbacks have experience in games like this. But Oklahoma's defense does figure to have a bounce-back game after struggling to contain LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina offense. The tackling will be better, and Florida's offense is in a bit of flux itself with Tramell Jones Jr. expected to make his second start of the season at quarterback and Florida's offensive line struggling in recent weeks. But the Gators still have plenty of talent, especially on the offensive side, and The Swamp is one of the toughest environments in college football. That's a tough position for a reeling team to be placed in. The game will be close into the second half but the Gators figure to pull away and hand Oklahoma its second consecutive defeat. Final: Florida 24, Oklahoma 14 Brady Trantham A new offensive coordinator doesn'tchange the fact that John Mateer is still QB1 at OU. Mateer gives Oklahoma their best shot in any game, but in 20 games as the Sooner signal caller, it is apparent that he simply isn't very good. A coaching change can, in theory, help him in spots, but if OU needs their QB to make a play in a tight game, chances are he will make that play - just for the other team. Florida sticks to the run and gets Oklahoma on a few explosives and rides it to an easy win. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss’ 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. “Not season-ending,” Golding said of Kutas’ injury in his weekly presser. “Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn’t seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. Ole Miss is 3-0 against the Sooners, who are trying to build on a 23-7 win over Florida . A win would also keep Oklahoma's bowl streak alive. Brown initially suffered the injury in the Gators win over Ole Miss on September 26 and was listed on the first SEC Availability Report on Wednesday as doubtful. Bailey Stockton (foot), who began the week as questionable and was upgraded to probable on Friday, will play against OU. Stockton has not missed a game yet this season despite nagging injuries. He's coming off an 8 catch, 76 yard performance in the 27-8 defeat to Georgia. Florida already ruled out four players on Wednesday for Saturday's game. Defensive tackle Jeremiah McCloud was suspended for "conduct detrimental to the team." Starting right tackle Emeka Ugorji is out, along with linebacker Jaden Robinson and tight end Evan Cheica. home.headline: Florida's latest injury report has Vernell Brown III out vs Oklahoma
home.blurb: Florida's latest injury report has Vernell Brown III out vs Oklahoma - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Florida's latest injury report has Vernell Brown III out vs Oklahoma The biggest change for Jon Sumrall's squad is the downgrade of wide receiver Vernell Brown III from questionable to out for Saturday. Brown will miss his fifth straight game with a grade-1 PCL strain that he suffered against Ole Miss in Week 4; it was re-aggravated ahead of last week's Georgia game. "So he was not available at practice today," Jon Sumrall said on Monday . "I really don't have a really strong feeling on timeline because everything early in the week last week was trending really positively until the setback on Wednesday. It sucks. It sucks for him. He's working like hell to try to get back. He's frustrated." The four others listed as out for the showdown in the Swamp are defensive lineman Jeramiah McCloud, tight end Evan Chieca, offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji and linebacker Jaden Robinson. McCloud is out due to a suspension, according to Swamp247 , while Robinson missed his first game of the season last week against Georgia. The good news is that the other two on the availability report — wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo — have been upgraded from questionable to probable. Both players were initially listed as doubtful last week; they ended up playing against Georgia. Offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis remains listed as doubtful, while defensive back Peyton Bowen is listed as questionable; wide receiver Elijah Thomas and defensive lineman Kenny Ozowalu are listed as probable. Wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, defensive back Eli Bowen, tight end Rocky Beers and offensive lineman Jake Maikkula are now cleared to play.
